definition_zh: 发展过程；开发流程（事物从早期形态逐步推进到成形或成熟的一连串阶段）
definition_en: the sequence of stages through which something grows, is built, or is brought to a finished form
core_image: 一面长墙上钉着排成一列的图纸，从潦草草图、分解图到能开动的样机，每一格都按着一枚进度图钉
scene: 实验室的长墙上钉着一排图纸，从最初的潦草草图一直排到成型的样机。The development process moved from a rough sketch to a working prototype in eighteen months.
sceneCN: 这里指「事物从早期形态逐步推进到成形的连续阶段」（第 1 个义项：从初步构想到成形的整体推进过程）；句意为这一推进过程在十八个月里从粗草图走到了能运转的原型。可辨识物件：长墙、图纸、进度图钉、样机。

pos.zh: 发展过程；开发流程（可数）

collocations.phrase: the development process of a vaccine

senses.title: Growth from an early to a mature state
senses.titleCN: 从初期到成熟的整体生长过程
senses.definition: the whole sequence by which something grows from an early condition to a mature one
senses.definitionCN: 事物从早期状态走向成熟状态的全过程
senses.example: The development process of a coral reef spans centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 珊瑚礁的生长过程跨越数百年。
senses.why: development began as the act of unfolding something rolled up, so the word naturally names a thing opening out over time.
senses.whyCN: 发展一词本指把卷起之物摊开，因此天然用来指事物随时间展开。

senses.title: The staged work of making a product
senses.titleCN: 制造产品时按阶段推进的工作
senses.definition: the ordered stages of designing, building and testing a new product before it reaches users
senses.definitionCN: 新产品在交付使用之前，依次经历设计、制造与测试的有序阶段
senses.example: The engineers shortened the development process by testing parts earlier.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师提前测试部件，从而缩短了产品开发流程。
senses.why: once industry needed a word for work that unfolds in steps, the older idea of unfolding was applied to factories.
senses.whyCN: 工业需要指称按步骤展开的工作，于是「展开」的旧义被移用到厂房里。

senses.title: The lifecycle of a piece of software
senses.titleCN: 软件从需求到维护的完整生命周期
senses.definition: the cycle of specifying, coding, testing, releasing and maintaining a program
senses.definitionCN: 程序从确定需求、编写代码、测试、发布到维护的循环
senses.example: Their development process includes a review before every release.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的开发流程在每次发布前都包含一次评审。
senses.why: software projects made the stages explicit and repeatable, so the phrase became a technical label.
senses.whyCN: 软件项目把各阶段明确化、可重复化，这个短语于是成了技术标签。

senses.title: Structural change in an economy or region
senses.titleCN: 经济或地区长期的结构性变化
senses.definition: the long sequence of changes by which an economy, city or region alters its structure
senses.definitionCN: 经济、城市或地区改变自身结构的长期变化序列
senses.example: Road building was one step in the region's development process.
senses.exampleCN: 修路是这个地区发展过程中的一步。
senses.why: economists borrowed the word because a region is said to grow much as a living thing does.
senses.whyCN: 经济学家借用了这个词，因为一个地区也被说成像生物那样生长。

senses.title: A child's course of maturing
senses.definition: the course through which a child's body, speech and understanding mature
senses.definitionCN: 儿童的身体、语言与理解力逐步成熟的历程
senses.example: Teachers record each child's development process in a portfolio.
senses.exampleCN: 教师用成长档案记录每个孩子的发展过程。
senses.why: psychology kept the biological reading of unfolding and applied it to the mind.
senses.whyCN: 心理学保留了「展开」的生物学含义，并把它用于心智。

senses.title: The steps by which a plan is worked out
senses.titleCN: 计划或协议逐步成形所经过的步骤
senses.definition: the series of talks and revisions through which a plan or agreement takes shape
senses.definitionCN: 计划或协议通过一连串商谈与修改而逐步成形
senses.example: The peace talks were a slow development process with many drafts.
senses.exampleCN: 和平谈判是一个经过许多草案的缓慢推进过程。
senses.why: the phrase extends the factory image to any piece of work that is built rather than found.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语把工厂图景扩展到一切需要「做出来」而非「现成得到」的工作。

senses.title: A repeating cycle of drafting and revision
senses.titleCN: 起草、试用、修改的反复循环
senses.definition: a loop in which a draft is tried, criticized and improved until it is accepted
senses.definitionCN: 草稿经过试用、批评与改进直到被接受的循环
senses.example: The handbook went through three rounds of the development process.
senses.exampleCN: 这本手册经历了三轮反复修改的流程。
senses.why: modern design treats the process as a loop rather than a line, which the phrase easily accommodates.
senses.whyCN: 现代设计把过程看成循环而非直线，这个短语正好容纳这种理解。

senses.title: Building the capacity of an organization
senses.titleCN: 组织逐步建立规则与能力的过程
senses.definition: the staged work of giving an organization the rules, staff and habits it needs to last
senses.definitionCN: 让一个组织获得长期存续所需的规则、人员与习惯的分阶段工作
senses.example: Donors funded the development process of the local health office.
senses.exampleCN: 捐助方资助了当地卫生机构的建设过程。
senses.why: development aid made the word common for institutions, not only for things.
senses.whyCN: 发展援助使这个词不只用于物件，也用于机构建设。

intro.en: Development process joins development, from Old French desveloper 'to unwrap, unfurl', and process, from Latin processus 'a going forward'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个词由表「发展」与表「过程」的两个名词组合而成：前者出自古法语 desveloper「解开、展开」，后者出自拉丁 processus「向前行进」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Desveloper meant 'to unwrap, unfurl, disclose'. It was built with a negative prefix plus a verb probably meaning 'to wrap', and that second element is the uncertain part.
items.cn: desveloper 意为「解开、展开、显露」，由否定前缀加一个大概意为「包裹」的动词构成，不确定的正是后一部分。

items.en: Processus 'a going forward, advance' came from procedere, pro- 'forward' plus cedere 'to go, to yield'.
items.cn: processus「向前行进、推进」出自 procedere，即 pro-「向前」加 cedere「走、让」。

items.en: English took process in the fourteenth century and development in the sixteenth, at first meaning the act of unfolding or disclosing.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪借入「过程」一词，十六世纪借入「发展」一词，后者最初指展开或显露的动作。

items.en: From the nineteenth century development was applied to land, resources and industry, where growth is planned rather than natural.
items.cn: 从十九世纪起，「发展」一词被用于土地、资源与工业，那里的成长是被规划的而非自然的。

items.en: The two nouns were joined in the twentieth century, when project management needed a name for work that advances in ordered stages.
items.cn: 两个名词在二十世纪合为一体，当时项目管理需要一个名称来指按有序阶段推进的工作。

items.en: Source uncertain: the pre-French origin of the 'wrap' element is not established, and any Frankish or Germanic form proposed for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定：那个表「包裹」的成分在法语之前的来源未获证明，凡为其提出的法兰克或日耳曼语形式均属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds words built from the same stems that are easily mistaken; group two holds near neighbours that name a sequence without naming growth.
note.cn: 第一组是由同一词干构成、容易看错的词；第二组是语义相近、但只说顺序不说生长的词。

entries.definition: Names growth or the built result; it lacks the explicit step-by-step frame that the full phrase supplies.
entries.definitionCN: 单指生长或建设成果，缺少完整短语所提供的分步框架。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to grow or to build up; the process is what the verb produces over time.
entries.definitionCN: 指生长或逐步建成的动词；过程正是这个动词随时间产生的产物。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning 'relating to development', common in biology and psychology, not a synonym of the phrase.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「与发育有关的」形容词，常用于生物学与心理学，并非该短语的同义词。

entries.definition: Names the person or company that carries out building work, so it is an agent rather than a sequence.
entries.definitionCN: 指实施建设的人或公司，是施动者而不是一个序列。

entries.definition: A prescribed order for doing something; it stresses rules, while the phrase stresses growth.
entries.definitionCN: 指办事的规定顺序，强调规则，而该短语强调生长。

entries.definition: The full span from birth or launch to end; it is close but usually names a closed loop.
entries.definitionCN: 指从诞生或推出到终结的全程，意思接近，但通常指闭合循环。

entries.definition: A forward movement through stages, without implying that the thing itself is being built.
entries.definitionCN: 指逐阶段向前推进，不含「事物本身被建造」的意思。

entries.definition: Slow change over a long time, often without a planner; the phrase usually implies deliberate work.
entries.definitionCN: 指长时间内的缓慢变化，常无规划者；该短语通常含有刻意推动之意。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real related words, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实相关词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Two real nouns sit inside the phrase: one for growth, one for a forward march.
normal.cn: 短语里含两个真实名词：一个表生长，一个表向前推进。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the technical uses: product development, software development.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出技术用法：产品开发、软件开发。

normal.en: The family runs develop, developer, developmental, developmentally.
normal.cn: 同族包括「发展」「开发者」「发育的」「在发育方面」。

normal.en: The second noun shares its root with proceed and procedure.
normal.cn: 第二个名词与「继续进行」「程序」共享同一词根。

normal.en: A wall chart with dated pins is the clearest picture of the phrase.
normal.cn: 钉着日期图钉的墙面进度图，是这个短语最清楚的画面。

abstract.en: Picture a rolled carpet slowly opened across a floor, room by room.
abstract.cn: 想象一卷地毯在地板上慢慢展开，一个房间接一个房间。

abstract.en: Picture a seed that must pass through soil, shoot and leaf before it is a plant.
abstract.cn: 想象一粒种子必须经过土、芽、叶，才成为一株植物。

abstract.en: Picture a relay race where each runner may not start before the last hand-off.
abstract.cn: 想象一场接力赛，每一棒都必须等上一棒交完才能起跑。

examples.en: The development process for the new battery took four years and three prototypes.
examples.cn: 新电池的开发过程历时四年，做了三台原型。

examples.en: Reviewers are invited into the development process before the design is frozen.
examples.cn: 评审者会在设计定稿之前被引入开发流程。

examples.en: A region's development process rarely follows a single straight line.
examples.cn: 一个地区的发展过程很少沿着一条直线走。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「底外乐普门特」加「破塞斯」——底下外面都乐着进门，一步一步把东西做出来。

root: development 出自古法语 desveloper「展开」，其表「包裹」的成分来源不确定；process 出自拉丁 processus「向前行进」，由 pro-「向前」与 cedere「走」构成。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one shape: something is opened out step by step, and the same shape is then given to products, software, economies, children, plans, repeated drafts and organizations.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个形状展开：某物被一步一步摊开，这个形状随后被赋予产品、软件、经济、儿童、计划、反复草稿与组织。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wall chart whose dated pins march from a rough sketch to a finished machine.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张墙面进度图，日期图钉从潦草草图一路排到成型的机器。

branches.en: GROWTH ITSELF: the phrase first names a thing opening out over time, with no factory in sight.
branches.cn: 生长本身：这个短语先指事物随时间展开，画面里还没有工厂。

branches.en: MAKING THINGS: product work and software work turn the sequence into a managed pipeline.
branches.cn: 制造物件：产品工作与软件工作把序列变成可管理的流水线。

branches.en: WHOLE REGIONS: an economy or city is said to grow the way a living body grows.
branches.cn: 整片地区：经济或城市被说成像生物体那样生长。

branches.en: MINDS AND PLANS: a child and a draft both move forward by steps that can be observed.
branches.cn: 心智与计划：孩子与草稿都按可观察的步骤向前。

branches.en: LOOPS AND BODIES: revision repeats the steps, and an organization acquires them as habits.
branches.cn: 循环与机构：修改让步骤重复，而一个组织把步骤沉淀为习惯。

intro.en: The phrase is built from two ordinary English nouns, so its parts can be read through the prefixes and roots that also build a large family.
intro.cn: 这个短语由两个普通英语名词构成，其各部分可通过同样构成一大族词的前缀与词根来读。

latinIntro.en: Latin cedere 'to go, yield' supplies proceed, procedure and process; the first noun goes back to a French verb whose second element is uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 cedere「走、让」衍生出「继续进行」「程序」与「过程」；第一个名词则上溯到一个法语动词，其后一成分来源不确定。

items.example: The prefix turns a wrapping action into an unwrapping one.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把「包裹」的动作变成「解开」。

items.example: Its origin is not established, so no older form can be quoted as fact.
items.exampleCN: 其来源未获证明，因此不能把任何更早的形式当作事实引用。

items.example: The team developed the sensor over three winters.
items.exampleCN: 团队用了三个冬天研发出这个传感器。

items.example: Housing development changed the edge of the town.
items.exampleCN: 住宅建设改变了小镇的边缘。

items.example: The clinic tracks developmental milestones.
items.exampleCN: 诊所追踪发育里程碑。

items.meaning: a person or firm that builds
items.example: The developer kept the old trees on the site.
items.exampleCN: 开发商保留了地块上的老树。

items.example: The process takes six working days.
items.exampleCN: 这个流程需要六个工作日。

items.example: Work proceeded in stages after the permit.
items.exampleCN: 拿到许可后，工程分阶段推进。

definition_zh: 制度化；收容安置（把某种做法固定为公认制度，或把人送入长期照护机构）
definition_en: the process by which a practice or organization becomes an accepted institution, or the act of placing someone in an institution
core_image: 一间挂着机构铭牌的旧楼，门口新钉的规章牌与一摞入住登记册并排
scene: 养老院的走廊上，护士站桌面并排放着登记册与一摞新印的规章。Years of policy work led to the institutionalization of elder care across the province.
sceneCN: 这里指「某种做法被固定为常设制度的过程」（第 1 个义项：由临时安排转为稳定制度）；句意为多年的政策工作使全省的养老照护走向制度化。可辨识物件：走廊、登记册、规章、护士站桌面。

pos.zh: 制度化；收容安置（不可数；指具体一次安置时可加不定冠词）

derivatives.zh: 已制度化的；长期住在机构里的
去机构化；减少收容安置

senses.title: A practice becoming an accepted institution
senses.titleCN: 某种做法成为公认制度
senses.definition: the process by which a practice, role or organization comes to be accepted as a permanent part of society
senses.definitionCN: 某种做法、角色或组织被承认为社会常设组成部分的过程
senses.example: The institutionalization of public schooling took most of the nineteenth century.
senses.exampleCN: 公共学校教育的制度化用了十九世纪的大半时间。
senses.why: the noun simply names the act of making something an institution, so the process and the result share one form.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词直接指「使某物成为制度」的动作，过程与结果共用一词。

senses.title: Placing a person in a residential institution
senses.titleCN: 把个人送入长期照护机构
senses.definition: the act of arranging for someone to live in a hospital, home or other residential institution
senses.definitionCN: 安排某人住进医院、养护院或其他居住性机构的举动
senses.example: The family delayed institutionalization until home care became impossible.
senses.exampleCN: 这家人一直拖到居家照护无法维持，才把老人送进机构。
senses.why: care systems borrowed the word because a placement is also a formal, recorded arrangement.
senses.whyCN: 照护体系借用这个词，因为安置同样是一种正式且有记录的安排。

senses.title: The state of long confinement
senses.titleCN: 长期待在机构中而形成的依赖状态
senses.definition: the condition of living so long under institutional routine that everyday independence is lost
senses.definitionCN: 因长期处于机构日常管理之中而失去日常生活自主的状态
senses.example: Critics warned that long institutionalization would weaken residents' daily skills.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者警告说，长期机构生活会使住养者的日常能力退化。
senses.why: the same noun shifts from the act of placing to the condition that the placement produces.
senses.whyCN: 同一个名词从「安置的动作」转为「安置造成的状态」。

senses.title: Norms becoming taken for granted
senses.titleCN: 规范被视为理所当然的社会学过程
senses.definition: in sociology, the process by which shared rules become so familiar that people stop questioning them
senses.definitionCN: 在社会学中，共同规则变得极为熟悉、以致人们不再质疑的过程
senses.example: The study traced the institutionalization of punctuality in factory life.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究追踪了守时观念在工厂生活中的制度化。
senses.why: sociology needed a word for ideas hardening into background assumptions, and reused the legal term.
senses.whyCN: 社会学需要指称观念固化为背景预设的词，于是复用了法律术语。

senses.title: Formalizing an organization
senses.titleCN: 给组织定规章、设岗位、立预算
senses.definition: the work of giving an organization written rules, defined offices and a stable budget
senses.definitionCN: 为一个组织建立成文规章、明确职位与稳定预算的工作
senses.example: Grant money paid for the institutionalization of the village committee.
senses.exampleCN: 拨款资助了村委会的制度化建设。
senses.why: an organization that acquires rules and offices has literally become an institution in the everyday sense.
senses.whyCN: 一个获得规章与职位的组织，在日常意义上确实成了「机构」。

senses.title: Writing an arrangement into law
senses.titleCN: 把某种安排写进法律或条例
senses.definition: the step by which an informal arrangement is codified in statutes or regulations
senses.definitionCN: 非正式安排被写入法规或条例的步骤
senses.example: The institutionalization of the ombudsman followed a ten-year campaign.
senses.exampleCN: 监察专员制度的确立源自一场长达十年的倡导。
senses.why: law makes the metaphor concrete: once written down, the institution can outlive the people who made it.
senses.whyCN: 法律让这个比喻落到实处：一旦写入文本，制度便能比创建者活得更久。

senses.title: An idea hardening into routine
senses.titleCN: 思想僵化为例行公事（贬义）
senses.definition: the negative sense in which a lively idea becomes rigid routine and blocks change
senses.definitionCN: 褒义转为贬义：有活力的想法固化为僵硬例行、阻碍改变
senses.example: Reviewers feared the institutionalization of the reform would drain its energy.
senses.exampleCN: 评审者担心改革一旦制度化，就会耗尽它的活力。
senses.why: the word's neutral process reading acquired a critical edge because institutions are also seen as slow and self-protecting.
senses.whyCN: 这个词中性的「过程」义带上批判色彩，因为机构也被视为迟缓而自我维护。

senses.title: Standard adoption by an established body
senses.titleCN: 由权威机构采纳并标准化
senses.definition: the step by which a method is adopted and standardized by universities, agencies or professional bodies
senses.definitionCN: 某种方法被大学、政府机关或行业团体采纳并标准化的步骤
senses.example: The institutionalization of the peer review system changed how papers were judged.
senses.exampleCN: 同行评审的制度化改变了论文的评判方式。
senses.why: adoption by a recognized body is the everyday test of whether a practice has become an institution.
senses.whyCN: 被权威机构采纳，是判断一种做法是否已成为制度的日常标准。

intro.en: Institutionalization is English institution plus the Latin-derived endings -al, -ize and -ation. Institution goes back to Latin instituere 'to set up'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个词是在英语「机构」一词上加若干拉丁来源后缀构成，而「机构」上溯拉丁 instituere「设立」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Statuere 'to set, place, cause to stand' came from stare 'to stand'. Its stem also gives statue, statute and stable ideas of standing firm.
items.cn: statuere「放置、使站立」出自 stare「站立」，其词干也构成「雕像」「法规」等表示「立住」的词。

items.en: In- 'in, on' plus statuere produced instituere 'to set up, establish, instruct', the verb behind both institute and institution.
items.cn: 前缀表「在内、在上」加 statuere 构成 instituere「设立、建立、教导」，是「研究所」与「机构」共同的动词来源。

items.en: Institutio named a setting up, an arrangement or a course of instruction; English took it as institution in the fifteenth century.
items.cn: institutio 指设立、安排或一套教导；英语在十五世纪把它借作「机构」一词。

items.en: English stacked -al (relating to), then -ize (to make), then -ation (the action), producing the long modern noun.
items.cn: 英语依次叠加三个后缀：表「相关」、表「使成为」、表「动作」，构成这个现代长名词。

items.en: Twentieth-century sociology gave the noun its neutral sense of norms becoming settled, and its critical sense of ideas hardening.
items.cn: 二十世纪社会学赋予它中性义「规范趋于稳定」，以及批判义「想法僵化」。

items.en: Source uncertain: the deeper pre-Latin origin of stare is not established, and the date at which the long noun was first used in sociology is not fixed.
items.cn: 来源不确定：stare 在拉丁语之前的更深来源未获证明，这个长名词首次用于社会学的年代亦无定论。

note.en: Group one holds words that share the same Latin stem and are easily confused; group two holds near neighbours that describe rules becoming fixed.
note.cn: 第一组共享同一拉丁词干、容易混淆；第二组指规则逐渐固定的近义词。

entries.definition: Names the body or the established rule itself; the long noun names the process of becoming one.
entries.definitionCN: 指机构或制度本身；长名词则指成为制度的过程。

entries.definition: An adjective describing what belongs to an institution, with no sense of a process.
entries.definitionCN: 描述属于某一机构的形容词，不含过程义。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to make something an institution or to place someone in one; the noun is its action.
entries.definitionCN: 指「使成为制度」或「送入机构」的动词，名词即其动作。

entries.definition: A noun for an organization or a verb for starting one; it is related but not the act of becoming established.
entries.definitionCN: 名词指研究院所，动词指创立；虽同源，却不表示「成为制度」的过程。

entries.definition: The act of writing rules down; it covers only one part of what institutionalization does.
entries.definitionCN: 指把规则写成文字，只覆盖制度化的一部分内容。

entries.definition: The act of founding something; it marks the beginning, while institutionalization marks the long settling.
entries.definitionCN: 指创立某物的动作，标记起点；制度化标记的是漫长的沉淀。

entries.definition: The spread of offices and procedures, usually with a critical tone; it is one path institutionalization can take.
entries.definitionCN: 指科室与程序的扩张，常带批评语气，是制度化可能走的一条路。

entries.definition: The arrangement of rules into a code; it is the legal step, not the whole social process.
entries.definitionCN: 指把规则整理成法典，是法律步骤，而非完整的社会过程。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real related words, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实相关词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Three suffixes stack in plain view: relating to, to make, the action.
normal.cn: 三个后缀层层叠加，顺序清楚：表相关、表使成为、表动作。

normal.en: The base noun and the verb differ by a single ending, so the pair is easy to keep.
normal.cn: 基础名词与动词只差一个词尾，因此这对词很容易记牢。

normal.en: Fixed phrases cluster around care: long-term institutionalization, delay institutionalization.
normal.cn: 固定搭配多围绕照护：长期收容安置、推迟收容安置。

normal.en: The family runs institute, institution, institutional, institutionalize, deinstitutionalization.
normal.cn: 同族包括「设立」「机构」「机构的」「使制度化」「去机构化」。

normal.en: Sociology uses it for norms, policy for organizations, medicine for placements.
normal.cn: 社会学用它讲规范，政策用它讲组织，医学用它讲安置。

abstract.en: Picture a tent that slowly acquires walls, a door and a nameplate.
abstract.cn: 想象一顶帐篷慢慢长出墙、门与门牌。

abstract.en: Picture a path worn into stone by enough feet that it stops being a choice.
abstract.cn: 想象一条被无数脚步磨进石头的路，走到它已不再是选择。

abstract.en: Picture a rule book heavy enough that nobody dares rewrite it.
abstract.cn: 想象一本厚重到没人敢改写的规则手册。

examples.en: The institutionalization of the exam system took two generations.
examples.cn: 考试制度的制度化用了两代人的时间。

examples.en: Her grandmother resisted institutionalization and stayed at home until ninety.
examples.cn: 她的祖母拒绝住进机构，一直在家住到九十岁。

examples.en: Too much institutionalization can turn a lively reform into paperwork.
examples.cn: 过度的制度化会把一场有活力的改革变成文书工作。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因斯提图深」加「耐了爱」——因着这套图景越挖越深，临时做法终于变成固定制度。

root: 拉丁 instituere「设立」由 in-「在内」与 statuere「放置、使站立」构成，后者出自 stare「站立」；英语 institution 加若干后缀构成这个长名词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses share one movement: something loose and temporary is fixed in place, whether that thing is a practice, an organization, a person or an idea.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项共享同一个动作：松散而临时之物被固定下来，无论那是做法、组织、人还是想法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a temporary arrangement receiving a permanent nameplate and a shelf of rules.
core.cn: 核心意象：一项临时安排被钉上永久铭牌，并配上一排规章。

branches.en: BECOMING ACCEPTED: a practice turns into an institution once a recognized body adopts it.
branches.cn: 获得承认：一种做法被权威机构采纳，便转为制度。

branches.en: WRITTEN DOWN: offices, budgets and statutes are the visible skeleton of the process.
branches.cn: 写成文字：职位、预算与法规是这一过程可见的骨架。

branches.en: PLACED INSIDE: a person can also be institutionalized, and long stay produces dependence.
branches.cn: 被安置其中：人也会被机构化，久住便生出依赖。

branches.en: BEHIND THE EYES: shared rules sink so deep that they stop being noticed.
branches.cn: 藏在目光之后：共同规则沉得太深，以致不再被察觉。

branches.en: THE COST: what settles can also stiffen, and a living idea becomes routine.
branches.cn: 代价：沉淀之物也会僵硬，活的想法变成例行。

intro.en: The word is a stack of Latin-derived endings on an English base, so it can be read outward from the base noun.
intro.cn: 这个词是在一个英语基础词上层层叠加拉丁来源后缀而成，可从基础名词向外读。

latinIntro.en: Latin stare 'to stand' and statuere 'to set up' underlie institution, institute, statute and statue; the ending -ation ultimately reflects a Latin action noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 stare「站立」与 statuere「设立」是「机构」「研究所」「法规」「雕像」的共同底层；表动作的后缀最终反映拉丁动作名词。

items.example: The prefix puts the setting inside the thing set up.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把「设立」的动作放进对象内部。

items.structure: Latin verb, 'to set, place, cause to stand'
items.example: The root supplies the image of a thing standing firm.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供「立稳」的画面。

items.example: The city instituted a noise code last year.
items.exampleCN: 该市去年设立了噪音条例。

items.example: The institution employs four hundred people.
items.exampleCN: 这个机构雇用了四百人。

items.example: Institutional review slowed the decision.
items.exampleCN: 机构内部的评审拖慢了决策。

items.example: They moved to institutionalize the arbitration service.
items.exampleCN: 他们着手把仲裁服务制度化。

items.meaning: already made institutional, or long resident
items.meaningCN: 已制度化的；长期住机构的
items.example: The practice is now fully institutionalized.
items.exampleCN: 这一做法如今已完全制度化。

items.meaning: the reversal of placement or of rules
items.meaningCN: 去机构化；减少收容安置
items.example: Policy shifted toward deinstitutionalization of mental care.
items.exampleCN: 政策转向减少精神照护的机构安置。

latinEntries.meaning: to set, place, cause to stand

definition_zh: 社会制度；社会机构（家庭、学校、宗教、法庭等由社会共同承认并长期沿用的组织或规则体系）
definition_en: an established organization or body of rules through which a society meets a basic need, such as the family, a school or a court
core_image: 广场四周并排立着教堂、学校与议事厅，台阶上有人在等待，每扇门上方都刻着同一枚旧纹章
scene: 小镇广场的四边围着教堂、学校和议事厅，人们从各自的门口进出。The village school became a social institution long before the state paid for it.
sceneCN: 这里指「社会共同承认并长期沿用的组织或规则体系」（第 1 个义项：为满足基本社会需要而设立的组织）；句意为这所村校早在国家出资之前就已成为一项社会制度。可辨识物件：广场、教堂、学校、议事厅、旧纹章。

pos.zh: 社会制度；社会机构（可数）

collocations.phrase: the family as a social institution

senses.title: An organization meeting a basic social need
senses.titleCN: 为满足基本社会需要而设的组织
senses.definition: an established organization that a society relies on to meet a basic need
senses.definitionCN: 社会为满足某项基本需要而依赖的常设组织
senses.example: The library is a social institution that serves everyone in the town.
senses.exampleCN: 图书馆是一项服务全镇所有人的社会机构。
senses.why: the phrase joins a word for companionship with a word for something set up, so it names a standing arrangement people share.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语把表「相伴」的词与表「设立」的词合在一起，指人们共同拥有的常设安排。

senses.title: The family as a foundational institution
senses.definition: the household as the first and most basic arrangement through which a society raises its young
senses.definitionCN: 社会抚养下一代所依靠的第一项、最基础的安排，即家庭
senses.example: Sociologists treat the family as the oldest social institution.
senses.exampleCN: 社会学家把家庭视为最古老的社会制度。
senses.why: the family is the clearest case where an everyday arrangement is also a recognized structure.
senses.whyCN: 家庭最能说明：日常安排同时也可以是被承认的结构。

senses.title: The school system
senses.definition: the organized system of schools and teaching that a society maintains
senses.definitionCN: 社会维持的学校与教学组织体系
senses.example: Compulsory schooling turned education into a national social institution.
senses.exampleCN: 义务教育使教育成为一项全国性的社会制度。
senses.why: schooling became a state duty, so the network that delivers it took the name of an institution.
senses.whyCN: 学校教育成为国家义务，承担它的网络因此获得了「制度」之名。

senses.title: An established religion
senses.definition: an organized religious body with recognized buildings, offices and rules
senses.definitionCN: 拥有被承认的场所、职位与规章的宗教组织
senses.example: The old temple remains a social institution as well as a place of worship.
senses.exampleCN: 这座古庙既是礼拜场所，也是一项社会制度。
senses.why: a faith with buildings and offices is an institution in the everyday sense as well as the sociological one.
senses.whyCN: 拥有场所与职位的信仰团体，在日常意义与社会学意义上都是制度。

senses.title: Courts and representative bodies
senses.definition: the legal and political bodies that settle disputes and make binding decisions
senses.definitionCN: 解决争端并作出有约束力决定的法律与政治机构
senses.example: A functioning court is a social institution in the strict sense.
senses.exampleCN: 运转正常的法庭是严格意义上的社会制度。
senses.why: courts settle disputes by recognized rules, which is the defining work of an institution.
senses.whyCN: 法庭依被承认的规则解决争端，而这正是制度的定义性工作。

senses.title: The market and property rules
senses.definition: the accepted rules of exchange, contract and ownership that make economic life predictable
senses.definitionCN: 使经济生活可预期的交换、契约与所有权规则
senses.example: Currency and contract are social institutions before they are economic tools.
senses.exampleCN: 货币与契约在成为经济工具之前，先已是社会制度。
senses.why: exchange needs stable expectations more than it needs buildings, so rules count as the institution.
senses.whyCN: 交换更需要稳定的预期而非建筑，因此规则本身就构成制度。

senses.title: A pattern of norms rather than a building
senses.titleCN: 作为规范格局而非实体建筑
senses.definition: a settled pattern of shared expectations that exists even without a single building
senses.definitionCN: 即使没有某座建筑也依然存在的共同期待格局
senses.example: Greeting customs are a social institution with no headquarters at all.
senses.exampleCN: 问候习俗是一项根本没有总部的社会制度。
senses.why: the sociological reading drops the building and keeps only the settled expectations.
senses.whyCN: 社会学的读法去掉建筑，只留下沉淀下来的共同期待。

senses.title: A body that shapes public opinion
senses.definition: an established press or broadcaster whose routines shape what a society considers news
senses.definitionCN: 其日常运作塑造社会「何为新闻」的既有报刊或广播机构
senses.example: The national broadcaster acts as a social institution during elections.
senses.exampleCN: 选举期间，这家全国广播机构起着社会制度的作用。
senses.why: a broadcaster's routines decide what counts as news, which is a basic need in a public.
senses.whyCN: 广播机构的日常运作决定什么算新闻，而这是公众的一项基本需要。

intro.en: Social institution joins social, from Latin socialis 'of companionship', and institution, from Latin instituere 'to set up'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个词由表「社会的」与表「机构」的两个名词组合而成：前者出自拉丁 socialis「相伴的」，后者出自拉丁 instituere「设立」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Socius meant 'companion, ally, partner'. Its deeper origin is uncertain; the link sometimes proposed with a root meaning 'to follow' is a reconstruction.
items.cn: socius 意为「同伴、盟友、合伙人」。其更深来源不确定；有人提出它与一个表「跟随」的词根有关，那属于重构形式。

items.en: The ending -alis built relational adjectives, so socialis meant 'of companions, of alliance' before English widened it to all of society.
items.cn: 表关系的拉丁形容词词尾构成这类形容词，因此 socialis 先指「同伴的、结盟的」，后来英语才把它扩展到整个社会。

items.en: In- plus statuere 'to set, cause to stand' produced instituere 'to set up, establish'.
items.cn: 前缀表「在内」加 statuere「放置、使站立」，构成 instituere「设立、建立」。

items.en: English formed institution in the fifteenth century from the Latin action noun, at first for an ordinance or an established body.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪由拉丁动作名词构成「机构」一词，最初指条例或已设立的机构。

items.en: Nineteenth-century sociology paired the two words to name the standing arrangements that outlast individuals.
items.cn: 十九世纪社会学把这两个词配对，用来指比个人活得更久的常设安排。

items.en: Source uncertain: the pre-Latin origin of socius is not established, so any older form quoted for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定：socius 在拉丁语之前的来源未获证明，凡为其引用的更早形式均属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds look-alike phrases and forms built from the same two stems; group two holds near neighbours that name organized life.
note.cn: 第一组是由同两个词干构成的形近短语与词形；第二组是描述组织化生活的近义词。

entries.definition: The arrangement of groups and ranks in a society; it is the shape institutions sit inside.
entries.definitionCN: 指社会中群体与层级的排列，是制度所嵌入的形态。

entries.definition: The condition in which rules are obeyed and life is predictable, rather than a named body.
entries.definitionCN: 指规则被遵守、生活可预期的状态，而非某个具名机构。

entries.definition: Used alone it may mean any organization, including a bank; the full phrase restricts it to society's basic arrangements.
entries.definitionCN: 单用时泛指任何机构，包括银行；完整短语把它限定为社会的基本安排。

entries.definition: The process by which people learn a society's norms; it is what institutions do to newcomers.
entries.definitionCN: 指人们习得社会规范的过程，是制度对新成员所做的事。

entries.definition: A structured group with a purpose; it lacks the phrase's implication of a basic social need.
entries.definitionCN: 指有目的的结构化团体，缺少该短语「满足基本社会需要」的含义。

entries.definition: Often names the existing holders of power, with a critical tone; it is narrower and more political.
entries.definitionCN: 常指在位的权力集团，带批评语气，范围更窄也更政治化。

entries.definition: A habitual practice handed down; it can be an institution's content but not the body itself.
entries.definitionCN: 指代代相传的习惯做法，可成为制度的内容，却不是机构本身。

entries.definition: A supporting structure of rules; it emphasizes design rather than social acceptance.
entries.definitionCN: 指支撑性的规则结构，强调设计，而非社会承认。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real related words, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实相关词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The adjective means 'of companions', which is exactly what a shared institution is.
normal.cn: 那个形容词意为「同伴的」，而共同制度正是同伴之间的事物。

normal.en: The second word means 'something set up', so the phrase is literally a standing arrangement.
normal.cn: 第二个词意为「被设立之物」，因此整个短语字面上就是一项常设安排。

normal.en: Fixed phrases pair it with family, school, religion and the market.
normal.cn: 固定搭配把它与家庭、学校、宗教、市场配对。

normal.en: The family runs society, social, socially, socialize, socialization, institution.
normal.cn: 同族包括「社会」「社会的」「在社会层面」「使社会化」「社会化」「机构」。

normal.en: Sociology contrasts institution with structure: the body versus the arrangement.
normal.cn: 社会学把「制度」与「结构」对照：前者是实体，后者是排列。

abstract.en: Picture four doors around one square, each opening onto the same old seal.
abstract.cn: 想象广场四周有四扇门，每扇都开向同一枚旧印章。

abstract.en: Picture a rule that people obey even when no official is watching.
abstract.cn: 想象一条即使没有官员看着、人们仍遵守的规则。

abstract.en: Picture a chair worn smooth by generations sitting in the same place.
abstract.cn: 想象一把椅子被一代代人坐在同一处，磨得发亮。

examples.en: The family is the social institution on which most others depend.
examples.cn: 家庭是大多数其他社会制度所依赖的那一项。

examples.en: A court that no one trusts has stopped working as a social institution.
examples.cn: 一个无人信任的法庭，已不再作为社会制度运转。

examples.en: Social institutions change more slowly than the people inside them.
examples.cn: 社会制度的变化比其中的人慢得多。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「搜受」加「因斯提图深」——大家一起搜罗并承受的那套深植的安排，就是社会制度。

root: social 出自拉丁 socialis「同伴的」，其词干 socius「同伴」的更深来源不确定；institution 出自拉丁 instituere「设立」，由 in- 与 statuere「放置、使站立」构成。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move outward from one idea: a basic need is met by an arrangement stable enough to be recognized, whether that arrangement is a family, a school, a faith, a court, a market, a custom or a broadcaster.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一个观念向外展开：某项基本需要由一种稳定到足以被承认的安排来满足，无论那是家庭、学校、信仰、法庭、市场、习俗还是广播机构。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: four doors around one square, each opening onto the same worn seal.
core.cn: 核心意象：广场四周的四扇门，每扇都通向同一枚磨旧的印章。

branches.en: THE DEFINITION: any established body that carries a basic need counts.
branches.cn: 定义本身：凡承担基本需要的常设组织都算。

branches.en: FIRST ARRANGEMENT: the household is the oldest and smallest case.
branches.cn: 最早的安排：家庭是最古老也最小的例子。

branches.en: TEACHING AND TELLING: schools form the young, broadcasters form what the public calls news.
branches.cn: 教导与告知：学校塑造年轻人，广播机构塑造公众所称的新闻。

branches.en: FAITH: a religious body is an institution in both the everyday and the strict sense.
branches.cn: 信仰：宗教团体在日常与严格意义上都是制度。

branches.en: ORDER WITHOUT A SINGLE ROOF: courts, market rules and customs all hold life steady, with or without walls.
branches.cn: 无需同一屋顶的秩序：法庭、市场规则与习俗都让生活稳定，无论有没有围墙。

intro.en: The phrase has two ordinary nouns, each with a productive Latin core, so it can be read from both halves.
intro.cn: 这个短语含两个普通名词，各自有一个能产的拉丁内核，因此可从两半分别读。

latinIntro.en: Latin socius and socialis supply the social family; Latin statuere and instituere supply the institution family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 socius 与 socialis 提供「社会」一族；拉丁 statuere 与 instituere 提供「机构」一族。

items.example: The root gives the idea of people standing together.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根带来「人们站在一起」的意思。

definition_zh: 教育；培养；教育学；（尤指）学校教育体系
definition_en: the process of teaching and learning, especially in schools, and the organized system that carries it out
core_image: 午后教室里的黑板、成排课桌与摊开的课本，窗台上摆着一只装满粉笔的旧铁盒
scene: 乡村学校的教室里，黑板擦得发亮，课桌排成几行，课本摊在桌面上。Public education gave every child in the valley a seat and a teacher.
sceneCN: 这里指「教与学的过程，尤指学校中的教育」（第 1 个义项：传授与习得知识的过程）；句意为公共教育让山谷里的每个孩子都有了座位和老师。可辨识物件：黑板、课桌、课本、粉笔盒。

pos.zh: 教育；培养；教育学（通常不可数；指一种教育经历时可加不定冠词）

forms.label: 形容词（教育的；教育性的）

senses.title: The process of teaching and learning
senses.definition: the activity through which knowledge, skills and habits are passed from one person to another
senses.definitionCN: 知识、技能与习惯在人与人之间传递的活动
senses.example: Good education begins with questions rather than answers.
senses.exampleCN: 好的教育从提问而不是从答案开始。
senses.why: the noun came from a verb meaning to bring up and rear, so its core is the whole act of raising someone's mind.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词出自表「养育、培养」的动词，其核心是把人的心智养成的整个动作。

senses.title: The school system
senses.definition: the organized network of schools, teachers, curricula and funding that a state or community maintains
senses.definitionCN: 国家或社区维持的学校、教师、课程与经费的组织网络
senses.example: Rural education improved after the new schools opened.
senses.exampleCN: 新学校开办之后，乡村教育得到改善。
senses.why: once schooling became a public service, the word shifted from the act to the machine that delivers it.
senses.whyCN: 一旦学校教育成为公共服务，这个词就从动作转向提供它的那台机器。

senses.title: A person's upbringing and formation
senses.titleCN: 一个人的教养与成长背景
senses.definition: the whole formation of a person's character and taste, including what happens outside school
senses.definitionCN: 一个人性格与品味所受的整体养成，包括校门之外的部分
senses.example: Her education at home was stricter than anything the school imposed.
senses.exampleCN: 她在家所受的教养比学校的一切要求都更严格。
senses.why: the older sense of rearing survives in phrases about a person's background rather than a system.
senses.whyCN: 较旧的「养育」义保留在谈论个人背景的短语里，而不指体系。

senses.title: The academic field of study
senses.definition: the discipline that studies how people learn and how teaching should be organized
senses.definitionCN: 研究人如何学习、教学应如何组织的学科
senses.example: She holds a doctorate in education from a state university.
senses.exampleCN: 她在一所州立大学取得教育学博士学位。
senses.why: a field of study takes the name of its object, which is why the discipline is simply called education.
senses.whyCN: 一门学科常以其研究对象命名，因此这门学科直接就叫「教育」。

senses.title: A level or stage of schooling
senses.titleCN: 某一阶段或层级的教育
senses.definition: a named stage such as primary, secondary or higher education
senses.definitionCN: 初等、中等或高等教育等具名阶段
senses.example: Fewer girls than boys continued into secondary education.
senses.exampleCN: 继续升入中等教育的女孩少于男孩。
senses.why: the single word covers each named stage, because a stage is only a portion of the whole process.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词覆盖每一个具名阶段，因为一个阶段只是整个过程中的一段。

senses.title: A public information campaign
senses.titleCN: 面向公众的宣传教育活动
senses.definition: an organized effort to teach the public about health, safety or civic matters
senses.definitionCN: 就健康、安全或公共事务向公众进行的有组织教育
senses.example: The clinic ran a road safety education week.
senses.exampleCN: 诊所办了一周的道路安全教育。
senses.why: the same word covers teaching that has no classroom, because the aim is still to change behaviour.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词也覆盖没有教室的教学，因为目的仍是改变行为。

senses.title: The teaching profession and its work
senses.definition: the occupation of teachers and the professional work they do
senses.definitionCN: 教师的职业及其专业工作
senses.example: She entered education after ten years in engineering.
senses.exampleCN: 她在工程界工作十年后进入教育行业。
senses.why: the activity became an industry with careers, so the word also names the trade itself.
senses.whyCN: 这项活动成为一个有职业路径的行业，因此这个词也指行业本身。

senses.title: The result: a cultivated mind
senses.titleCN: 教育的结果：被培养出的心智
senses.definition: the knowledge and judgement a person finally possesses as a result of learning
senses.definitionCN: 一个人因学习而最终拥有的知识与判断力
senses.example: His education showed in the way he listened before speaking.
senses.exampleCN: 他的教养体现在他先听后说的方式上。
senses.why: the word can name either the journey or what the traveller carries at the end.
senses.whyCN: 这个词既可指旅程，也可指旅人最终带着的东西。

intro.en: Education comes from Latin educatio 'a rearing, training', from educare 'to bring up, rear'. It reached English through French. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁 educatio「养育、培养」，其动词为 educare「抚养、培育」，经法语进入英语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Educare meant 'to bring up, rear, nurture'. It is generally connected with the idea of drawing out a person's capacities, though the exact pre-Latin shape is not established.
items.cn: educare 意为「抚养、培育、养育」，一般认为与「把人身上的能力引发出来」这一观念相关，但其拉丁语之前的确切形态未获证明。

items.en: Educere, ex- 'out' plus ducere 'to lead', meant 'to lead out'. The famous notion of education as leading a mind out rests on this second verb.
items.cn: educere 由 ex-「向外」加 ducere「引导」构成，意为「引出」。把教育理解为「把心智引出来」的著名说法，依据的正是这第二个动词。

items.en: Educatio named the rearing and training of a child. English took the noun through French with the same meaning.
items.cn: educatio 指对儿童的抚养与训练，英语经法语借入时保留了同一含义。

items.en: From the eighteenth century the word increasingly meant formal instruction in schools rather than upbringing at home.
items.cn: 从十八世纪起，这个词越来越多地指学校里的正式教学，而非家庭中的养育。

items.en: In the twentieth century education also became the name of the academic discipline that studies teaching and learning.
items.cn: 二十世纪，「教育」又成为研究教与学的学科的正式名称。

items.en: Source uncertain: whether the older verb meant 'nourish' or 'lead out' cannot be settled for the earliest layer, and the link sometimes drawn to a root meaning 'to lead' is a hypothesis.
items.cn: 来源不确定：最早一层究竟取「养育」还是「引出」，无法定论；有人把它与表「引导」的词根相连，那只是假说。

note.en: Group one holds forms from the same Latin verb that are constantly confused; group two holds near neighbours that name learning.
note.cn: 第一组是同一拉丁动词衍生、极易混淆的词形；第二组是表示学习的近义词。

entries.definition: To teach or bring up someone; the noun education names the whole activity or system, not a single act.
entries.definitionCN: 指教育或培养某人；名词则指整个活动或体系，而非单个动作。

entries.definition: Meaning 'relating to education' or 'instructive', as in an educational visit.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「与教育有关的」或「有教育意义的」，如一次有教育意义的参观。

entries.definition: Describes a person who has received education; it is a state, not the system.
entries.definitionCN: 描述受过教育的人，是一种状态，而非体系。

entries.definition: A teacher or someone who works in education; the ending marks the doer.
entries.definitionCN: 指教师或教育工作者，词尾标记施动者。

entries.definition: The formal instruction actually received in schools; it is the measurable part of education.
entries.definitionCN: 指在学校实际受到的正式教学，是教育中可测量的部分。

entries.definition: Practice aimed at a particular skill; it is narrower and usually has a task in view.
entries.definitionCN: 指针对某项技能的练习，范围更窄，通常有具体任务。

entries.definition: The knowledge or skill acquired; it names the result rather than the organized giving.
entries.definitionCN: 指获得的知识或技能，说的是结果而非有组织的传授。

entries.definition: Deliberate teaching of content, often in steps; it is a method within education.
entries.definitionCN: 指有步骤地教授内容，是教育之内的种方法。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real related words, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实相关词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The family runs educate, educated, educational, educator, educative.
normal.cn: 同族包括「教育」「受过教育的」「教育的」「教育者」「有教育作用的」。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the stages: primary, secondary and higher education.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出阶段：初等、中等与高等教育。

normal.en: One verb has two readings, nourish and lead out, and both survive in how people talk about teaching.
normal.cn: 同一个动词有「养育」与「引出」两种读法，两种都留在人们谈论教学的方式里。

normal.en: The same noun serves the activity, the system and the discipline.
normal.cn: 同一个名词兼指活动、体系与学科。

normal.en: A classroom with a board, desks and books is the easiest picture to hold.
normal.cn: 有黑板、课桌与书本的教室是最容易抓住的画面。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp being lit rather than a bucket being filled.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏灯被点亮，而不是一只桶被灌满。

abstract.en: Picture a seed given soil, water and time, then growing on its own.
abstract.cn: 想象一粒种子得到土、水与时间，然后自行生长。

abstract.en: Picture a path with several gates, each opened by a different stage of study.
abstract.cn: 想象一条有几道门的路径，每道门由不同的学习阶段打开。

examples.en: Education is the surest route out of poverty for a whole village.
examples.cn: 对一个村庄来说，教育是摆脱贫困最可靠的路。

examples.en: The ministry spends a third of its budget on basic education.
examples.cn: 该部把三分之一的预算投入基础教育。

examples.en: Her education taught her to read a contract before signing it.
examples.cn: 她所受的教育让她在签字前先读懂合同。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱丢开心」——把不懂的东西一点点丢掉，心就开了，这就是教育。

root: 拉丁 educare「抚养、培育」构成 educatio「养育、训练」；一般认为它与表「引出」的 educere 相关，但「引出说」属后世解释，最早一层含义不能定论。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one movement: a person is brought up, and that bringing-up is then organized into schools, stages, a profession and a discipline, until it finally names what the person carries away.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：一个人被养成人，这种养成随后被组织成学校、阶段、职业与学科，最后用来指那个人带走的东西。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lamp lit in a room rather than a bucket filled from outside.
core.cn: 核心意象：屋里被点亮的一盏灯，而不是从外面灌满的一只桶。

branches.en: THE ACT AND ITS FRUIT: teaching is both the journey and the judgement carried home.
branches.cn: 动作与果实：教学既是旅程，也是带回家的判断力。

branches.en: THE MACHINE AND THE TRADE: a system of schools needs a profession to run it.
branches.cn: 机器与行业：学校体系需要一支职业队伍来运转。

branches.en: BEFORE AND BEYOND SCHOOL: character is formed at home as much as in class.
branches.cn: 校门内外：性格在家里形成，不比在课堂上少。

branches.en: ORGANIZED KNOWLEDGE: a discipline studies education, while stages divide it.
branches.cn: 被组织起来的知识：一门学科研究教育，而阶段把教育分段。

branches.en: WITHOUT A CLASSROOM: campaigns teach the public where no desk exists.
branches.cn: 没有教室：宣传活动在无课桌处教育公众。

intro.en: The word is a Latin action noun whose verb also builds a compact English family, so it can be read from the verb outward.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁动作名词，其动词在英语里也构成一个紧凑词族，因此可从动词向外读。

latinIntro.en: Latin educare 'to rear' and educere 'to lead out' share the element ducere 'to lead'; educatio is the action noun built on the first.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 educare「养育」与 educere「引出」共享表「引导」的成分；educatio 是在前一个动词上构成的动作名词。

items.example: The prefix turns leading into a movement out of something.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把「引导」变成「从某处向外」的动作。

items.example: The root supplies the image of a guide walking ahead.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根带来「引路者走在前面」的画面。

items.example: The verb names the whole work of raising a child.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词指抚养孩子的全部工作。

items.example: They educate their children at home until six.
items.exampleCN: 孩子在六岁前由他们在家教育。

items.meaning: the act, system or result of teaching
items.example: Education changes what a family can imagine.
items.exampleCN: 教育改变一个家庭所能想象的东西。

items.example: The museum runs educational programs for schools.
items.exampleCN: 博物馆为学校开设教育项目。

items.example: The educator trained new teachers in the district.
items.exampleCN: 这位教育工作者在本区培训新教师。

items.example: Failure can be educative if it is examined.
items.exampleCN: 失败若被审视，也能起教育作用。

definition_zh: 读写能力；（某一领域的）基本素养与判断力；识字普及程度
definition_en: the ability to read and write, and the competence needed to understand and use information in a particular field
core_image: 一张旧书桌上摊开的识字课本，页边压着一支削短的铅笔，旁边是一份签过名字的登记表
scene: 夜校的桌上摊着识字课本，页边压着一支削短的铅笔。Adult literacy classes fill the church hall on Tuesdays and Thursdays.
sceneCN: 这里指「读写能力」（第 1 个义项：读书识字的基本能力）；句意为成人识字班每逢周二和周四坐满了教堂大厅。可辨识物件：识字课本、铅笔、登记表、长桌。

pos.zh: 读写能力；素养（通常不可数）

derivatives.zh: 识字的；有文化的 / 识字者

senses.title: The ability to read and write
senses.definition: the basic ability to read and write a short simple text
senses.definitionCN: 读懂并写出简短浅近文字的基本能力
senses.example: Literacy opens the first door that poverty had shut.
senses.exampleCN: 读写能力打开了贫困关上的第一道门。
senses.why: the noun was built on the Latin word for a letter of the alphabet, so its oldest content is simply knowing one's letters.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词建在拉丁语「字母」一词上，因此它最古老的内容就是「认识字母」。

senses.title: The measured level in a population
senses.titleCN: 一个人群中被统计的识字程度
senses.definition: the share of a population that can read and write, treated as a figure to be counted
senses.definitionCN: 能够读写者在人口中所占的比例，被当作可统计的数字
senses.example: Literacy in the province rose from half to four fifths in one generation.
senses.exampleCN: 这个省的识字水平在一代人之内从一半升至五分之四。
senses.why: once states began to measure the skill, the word also named the number rather than the ability.
senses.whyCN: 一旦国家开始测量这项技能，这个词也就指数字而非能力。

senses.title: Functional literacy for daily tasks
senses.titleCN: 应付日常事务的实用读写能力
senses.definition: the reading and writing needed to fill in forms, follow instructions and manage a household
senses.definitionCN: 填写表格、看懂指示、料理家务所需的读写能力
senses.example: The course targets functional literacy rather than exam skills.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课针对的是日常实用读写能力，而不是应试技巧。
senses.why: policy shifted focus from letters to use, so the old word acquired a practical measure.
senses.whyCN: 政策重心从「认字」转向「会用」，这个旧词由此带上实用尺度。

senses.title: Digital literacy
senses.titleCN: 使用数字工具与判断网络信息的能力
senses.definition: the ability to use computers and networks and to judge what one finds there
senses.definitionCN: 使用计算机与网络，并判断所见信息的能力
senses.example: Students need digital literacy before they can research online.
senses.exampleCN: 学生要先具备数字素养，才能在网络上做研究。
senses.why: the pattern of basic competence in a domain was extended from print to screens.
senses.whyCN: 「某领域的基本能力」这一模式从纸面扩展到了屏幕。

senses.title: Financial literacy
senses.titleCN: 看懂收支、利率与风险的能力
senses.definition: the ability to understand money, interest, debt and risk well enough to decide wisely
senses.definitionCN: 理解金钱、利率、债务与风险并据以明智决策的能力
senses.example: Schools now teach financial literacy alongside mathematics.
senses.exampleCN: 学校如今把金融素养与数学一起教。
senses.why: the same frame applies wherever a field has codes that outsiders cannot read.
senses.whyCN: 只要某领域有一套外人读不懂的规则，这个框架就适用。

senses.title: Media literacy
senses.titleCN: 识别媒体信息意图与可信度的能力
senses.definition: the ability to read how news and advertising are built, and to judge their reliability
senses.definitionCN: 看懂新闻与广告如何被构造，并判断其可信度的能力
senses.example: Media literacy helps readers notice what a headline leaves out.
senses.exampleCN: 媒体素养帮助读者察觉标题省略了什么。
senses.why: news and advertising are constructed texts, so reading them needs the same skill as reading print.
senses.whyCN: 新闻与广告都是被构造的文本，读懂它们需要与读印刷品相同的功夫。

senses.title: Cultural literacy
senses.titleCN: 共享文化常识的通晓程度
senses.definition: the shared background knowledge that lets people understand references and jokes
senses.definitionCN: 使人能理解典故与玩笑的共同背景知识
senses.example: Cultural literacy includes knowing why a certain date matters.
senses.exampleCN: 文化素养包括知道某个日期为何重要。
senses.why: the word widened from letters to the common stock of references a society assumes.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从「字母」扩展到社会默认人人共有的典故储备。

senses.title: Literacy in a specialized field
senses.titleCN: 某一专业领域的基本通晓
senses.definition: working knowledge of the basic ideas and vocabulary of a subject such as science or law
senses.definitionCN: 对科学、法律等学科的基本概念与术语具备可用知识
senses.example: Scientific literacy is now treated as part of general education.
senses.exampleCN: 科学素养如今被视为通识教育的一部分。
senses.why: a subject's basic vocabulary works like an alphabet, so the same word fits it.
senses.whyCN: 某学科的基本词汇就像一套字母，因此同一个词也适用于它。

intro.en: Literacy is English literate plus the noun ending -cy, and literate goes back to Latin litteratus 'lettered', built on littera 'letter of the alphabet'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个词是在英语形容词「识字的」上加名词后缀构成，而该形容词上溯拉丁 litteratus「识字的」，后者建于 littera「字母」之上。年代均为约数。

items.en: Littera meant a letter of the alphabet; in the plural it also meant a written message or writings in general. Its deeper origin is not established.
items.cn: littera 指字母；复数时也指书信或一般著作。其更深来源未获证明。

items.en: Litteratus meant 'marked with letters, lettered, learned', an adjective formed from the noun.
items.cn: litteratus 意为「写有字母的、识字的、有学问的」，是由该名词构成的形容词。

items.en: English borrowed the adjective in the fifteenth century, using it first for learned people and later for anyone able to read.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪借入这个形容词，先用于有学问的人，后用于任何能读书的人。

items.en: The noun is a nineteenth-century formation, made as the positive counterpart of illiteracy when mass schooling made the skill a public question.
items.cn: 这个名词是十九世纪的构词，作为「文盲状态」的反面说法而造，当时大众教育使识字成为公共议题。

items.en: From the late twentieth century the word was attached to new fields, giving digital, financial, media and scientific literacy.
items.cn: 从二十世纪后期起，这个词被挂到新的领域上，形成数字、金融、媒体与科学素养等说法。

items.en: Source uncertain: the pre-Latin origin of the word for a letter is unknown, and the exact first printed use of the modern noun is not fixed.
items.cn: 来源不确定：那个表「字母」的词在拉丁语之前的来源不明，这个现代名词最早的确切印刷书证亦无定论。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same letter-root that are easily swapped; group two holds neighbours naming competence.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「字母」词根、容易用错的词；第二组是表示能力的近义词。

entries.definition: Describes a person or society that can read; the noun names the ability itself.
entries.definitionCN: 描述能读写的个人或社会；名词则指能力本身。

entries.definition: The body of written works, or the published material on a subject; it is the product, not the ability.
entries.definitionCN: 指成体系的著作，或某主题的已发表文献；是产物而非能力。

entries.definition: Meaning 'following the exact words'; it shares the letter-root but has nothing to do with reading skill.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「照字面的」，虽共享「字母」词根，却与读写能力无关。

entries.definition: The lack of the ability; it is the negative noun built with a prefix of negation.
entries.definitionCN: 指缺乏这种能力，是用否定前缀构成的反面名词。

entries.definition: Basic competence with numbers, coined on the model of literacy.
entries.definitionCN: 指对数字的基本能力，仿照「读写能力」造出。

entries.definition: The broad process of schooling; literacy is one measurable part of it.
entries.definitionCN: 指广泛的学校教育过程；读写能力是其中可测量的一部分。

entries.definition: A general word for a high level of skill in something; it carries no link to letters.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指某项技能的高水平，不含与「字母」的联系。

entries.definition: The sufficiency to perform a task; it is broader and less measurable than literacy.
entries.definitionCN: 指足以完成任务的能力，范围更广，且不如读写能力那样可测量。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real related words, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实相关词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The root means 'letter', so the core of the word is literally knowing one's letters.
normal.cn: 词根意为「字母」，因此这个词的核心字面上就是「认识字母」。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the newer fields: digital, financial and media literacy.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出较新的领域：数字素养、金融素养与媒体素养。

normal.en: The noun pairs with its negative twin, one built with a prefix of denial.
normal.cn: 这个名词与它的否定孪生词配对，后者由否定前缀构成。

normal.en: The family runs literate, illiterate, literature, literal, literacy.
normal.cn: 同族包括「识字的」「不识字的」「文学」「字面的」「读写能力」。

normal.en: The phrase 'literacy campaign' keeps the public-policy sense visible.
normal.cn: 「扫盲运动」这一说法让公共政策义保持可见。

abstract.en: Picture a key that fits many doors but was cut for one lock first.
abstract.cn: 想象一把能开许多门的钥匙，最初却只为一把锁而削。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp that lets a reader walk through a dark room without falling.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏灯，让读者走过暗室而不摔倒。

abstract.en: Picture a currency accepted in every shop, learned one letter at a time.
abstract.cn: 想象一种每个店铺都收的货币，是一个字母一个字母学来的。

examples.en: Literacy among women rose fastest where evening classes were free.
examples.cn: 在夜校免费的地方，女性识字率上升最快。

examples.en: Digital literacy is now as basic as reading a timetable.
examples.cn: 数字素养如今已和看懂时刻表一样基础。

examples.en: The campaign cut adult illiteracy by half in six years.
examples.cn: 这场运动在六年内把成人文盲率降低了一半。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「里特乐西」——里里外外认得那些特小的字母，心里就乐，这就是读写能力。

root: 拉丁 littera「字母」构成形容词 litteratus「识字的」；英语先借入形容词，十九世纪再加名词后缀构成 literacy，作为「文盲状态」的反面说法。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses grow from one seed: knowing letters becomes the ability to read, then a number to count, then a set of practical competences that spread to screens, money, news and finally to any field with its own codes.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一粒种子长出：认识字母变成读写能力，再变成可统计的数字，随后成为一套实用能力，扩展到屏幕、金钱、新闻，最后延伸到任何有自身规则的专业领域。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a short pencil pressed on a page beside a signed form.
core.cn: 核心意象：一支削短的铅笔压在纸页上，旁边是一份签过名的表格。

branches.en: THE SEED: knowing letters is the oldest and simplest layer of the word.
branches.cn: 种子：认识字母是这个词最古老也最简单的一层。

branches.en: COUNTED: a state can turn the ability into a percentage, and the word follows.
branches.cn: 被计数：国家能把能力换算成百分比，词义也随之跟进。

branches.en: USING IT: forms and instructions on one side, a discipline's vocabulary on the other.
branches.cn: 会用：一边是表格与说明，另一边是某学科的专业词汇。

branches.en: NEW MEDIA: screens and headlines each demand a literacy of their own.
branches.cn: 新媒介：屏幕与标题各自要求一套自己的素养。

branches.en: CODES OF THE WORLD: money and shared culture are also systems one must learn to read.
branches.cn: 世界的密码：金钱与共同文化同样是必须学会读懂的体系。

intro.en: The word is a short English noun built on a Latin root for a letter, with a suffix of state or quality.
intro.cn: 这是一个简短的英语名词，建在拉丁语表「字母」的词根上，并带一个表状态或性质的后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin littera gives letter, letters and literature in English, while litteratus gives literate and, with a negating prefix, illiterate.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 littera 在英语里衍生出「字母」「书信」与「文学」，litteratus 则衍生出「识字的」，加上否定前缀又有「不识字的」。

items.meaning: a letter; writings in the plural
items.meaningCN: 字母；复数指书信或著作
items.example: The root names the smallest unit of written language.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根指书面语言的最小单位。

items.meaning: a written sign for a speech sound
items.example: A single letter can change a whole meaning.
items.exampleCN: 一个字母就能改变整个意思。

items.example: The village is almost wholly literate now.
items.exampleCN: 这个村子如今几乎人人识字。

items.meaning: the state of being able to read
items.example: Literacy was made a national target.
items.exampleCN: 识字被定为国家目标。

items.example: The forms were useless to illiterate tenants.
items.exampleCN: 这些表格对不识字的租户毫无用处。

items.example: She read the literature on soil erosion.
items.exampleCN: 她读了关于土壤侵蚀的文献。

items.example: A literal translation missed the joke.
items.exampleCN: 直译丢掉了那个玩笑。

items.example: He was a man of letters in the old sense.
items.exampleCN: 在旧时的意义上，他是个文人。

definition_zh: 识字的；有文化的；通晓某领域的（也可作名词：识字的人）
definition_en: able to read and write, educated, or knowledgeable about a particular subject
core_image: 一位老人坐在窗边的木桌前，手指按着一页密密麻麻的文字，桌角摞着几本翻旧的书
scene: 窗边的木桌前，一位老人用手指按着一页密密麻麻的文字，桌上摞着翻旧的书。By eighty she was still a keen reader, wholly literate and never without a book.
sceneCN: 这里指「具备读写能力」（第 1 个义项：能够读书写字）；句意为她到八十岁仍爱读书，完全识字，手边从不缺书。可辨识物件：木桌、书页、旧书、窗光。

pos.zh: 识字的；有文化的；通晓的
识字的人；有文化的人（较少用）

senses.title: Able to read and write
senses.definition: having the basic ability to read and write simple texts
senses.definitionCN: 具备读懂并写出浅近文字的基本能力
senses.example: Only half the adults in the district were literate in nineteen fifty.
senses.exampleCN: 一九五零年，这个区只有一半成年人识字。
senses.why: the adjective is the direct Latin word for 'lettered', so its first sense is the plain possession of letters.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词直接来自拉丁语「写有字母的」，因此第一义就是字面意义上的「认得字母」。

senses.title: Educated and well read
senses.definition: having a broad education and familiarity with serious writing
senses.definitionCN: 受过良好教育并熟悉严肃著作
senses.example: Her letters show a literate mind at work.
senses.exampleCN: 她的书信显出一个有教养的心灵在运转。
senses.why: knowing letters grew into knowing books, and knowing books grew into general cultivation.
senses.whyCN: 「认得字母」长成「读过书」，「读过书」又长成「有教养」。

senses.title: Functionally literate in daily life
senses.titleCN: 能应付日常事务的书信能力
senses.definition: able to handle forms, instructions and ordinary paperwork without help
senses.definitionCN: 无需他人帮助即可处理表格、说明与日常文书
senses.example: Applicants must be functionally literate to fill the form alone.
senses.exampleCN: 申请人须具备实用读写能力，才能独立填表。
senses.why: administration turned the broad ability into a practical threshold.
senses.whyCN: 行政事务把宽泛的能力变成一个实用门槛。

senses.title: Computer literate
senses.titleCN: 会用计算机与常用软件
senses.definition: confident with computers and common software, usually in the fixed phrase computer literate
senses.definitionCN: 能熟练使用计算机与常用软件，通常见于「会用电脑」这一固定说法
senses.example: New staff must be computer literate before they start.
senses.exampleCN: 新员工入职前必须会用电脑。
senses.why: a computer's keyboard and menus became the new letters, so the old adjective was reused.
senses.whyCN: 计算机的键盘与菜单成了新的「字母」，这个旧形容词因此被复用。

senses.title: Literate in a subject
senses.definition: knowing enough of a subject's language to read and judge its material
senses.definitionCN: 掌握某学科的语言，足以阅读并判断其材料
senses.example: Voters should be economically literate enough to read a budget.
senses.exampleCN: 选民应具备足够的经济素养，能读懂一份预算。
senses.why: the pattern 'knows the letters of a field' is reused for every specialty.
senses.whyCN: 「认得某领域的字母」这一模式被复用到每一门专业上。

senses.title: A literate style of writing
senses.definition: describing prose that is clear, polished and clearly the work of a reader
senses.definitionCN: 形容文字清楚、打磨过、明显出自读书人之手
senses.example: The report was literate without being showy.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告写得有文气，却不炫耀。
senses.why: the adjective can describe the product as well as the person, because style was seen as the mark of letters.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词也能形容作品而非人，因为文风被视为读书的印记。

senses.title: A largely literate population
senses.definition: describing a society or group in which most adults can read and write
senses.definitionCN: 描述多数成年人都能读写的群体或社会
senses.example: A literate workforce adapted quickly to printed instructions.
senses.exampleCN: 识字的劳动力能迅速适应书面说明。
senses.why: the adjective can describe a whole population, because it was originally a description of persons.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词最初描述个人，因此也能描述整个人口。

senses.title: A person who can read (noun use)
senses.definition: a person who has learned to read and write, especially in accounts of schooling
senses.definitionCN: 已学会读写的人，尤见于教育记述中
senses.example: The program graduated eight hundred literates in its first year.
senses.exampleCN: 该项目第一年培养出八百名识字者。
senses.why: English often turns an adjective into a noun for the people who bear the quality.
senses.whyCN: 英语常把形容词直接用作名词，指具备该性质的人。

intro.en: Literate comes from Latin litteratus 'marked with letters, learned', an adjective on littera 'letter'. English borrowed it in the fifteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁 litteratus「写有字母的、有学问的」，该形容词建于 littera「字母」之上，十五世纪进入英语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Littera named a letter of the alphabet, and in the plural a letter, a document or writings. The deeper origin of the word is not established.
items.cn: littera 指字母，复数指书信、文书或著作。这个词更深的来源未获证明。

items.en: The ending -atus formed adjectives of possession, so litteratus meant 'furnished with letters', hence able to read and, by extension, learned.
items.cn: 表「具有」的拉丁形容词词尾构成这类形容词，因此 litteratus 意为「带有字母的」，引申为能读书，再引申为有学问。

items.en: English took the adjective in the fifteenth century, at first describing clergy and scholars rather than ordinary readers.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪借入这个形容词，最初描述神职人员与学者，而非普通读者。

items.en: With mass printing and schooling the word spread to anyone who could read, and to whole populations.
items.cn: 随着大众印刷与学校教育普及，这个词扩展到任何能读书的人，也用于整个人口。

items.en: Late twentieth-century usage produced computer literate and financially literate, applying the adjective to specific competences.
items.cn: 二十世纪后期的用法产生了「会用电脑的」「懂金融的」等说法，把这个形容词用于具体能力。

items.en: Source uncertain: the pre-Latin origin of the letter-word is unknown, and no single first recorded use of the modern everyday sense can be verified.
items.cn: 来源不确定：那个表「字母」的词在拉丁语之前的来源不明，现代日常义的最早书证亦无法确证。

note.en: Group one holds words and forms from the same root that are often confused; group two holds adjectives describing an educated person.
note.cn: 第一组是同根而常被混淆的词形；第二组是描述受教育者的形容词。

entries.definition: The ability itself, not the person who has it; it is what a literate person possesses.
entries.definitionCN: 指能力本身，而非拥有能力的人；它是识字者所拥有的东西。

entries.definition: Meaning 'word for word'; it looks close but describes translation, not reading ability.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「逐字的」，外形接近，却描述翻译方式而非读写能力。

entries.definition: Relating to literature as an art; a literate person need not be literary.
entries.definitionCN: 指与作为艺术的文学有关；识字的人未必有文学趣味。

entries.definition: Unable to read or write; it is the exact opposite, built with a prefix of denial.
entries.definitionCN: 指不能读写，是它的确切反义，由否定前缀构成。

entries.definition: Having had formal schooling; it says nothing about the bare ability to read.
entries.definitionCN: 指受过正规学校教育，不涉及最基本的读写能力。

entries.definition: An older word for widely read and scholarly; it is close in meaning but dated in tone.
entries.definitionCN: 较旧的说法，指博览而博学，意思接近但语气古旧。

entries.definition: Having read widely in serious books; it is narrower than a general literate upbringing.
entries.definitionCN: 指广泛读过严肃书籍，范围比一般「有文化」窄。

entries.definition: Comfortable with numbers and quantitative reasoning, coined on the model of literate.
entries.definitionCN: 指熟悉数字与定量推理，仿「识字的」造出。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real related words, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实相关词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The ending means 'furnished with', so the word literally says a person is furnished with letters.
normal.cn: 那个词尾意为「带有」，因此这个词字面上是说一个人「带着字母」。

normal.en: Fixed phrases add the specialty: computer literate, financially literate.
normal.cn: 固定搭配补上专业领域：会用电脑、懂金融。

normal.en: The positive and negative forms differ only by a prefix of denial.
normal.cn: 肯定式与否定式只差一个否定前缀。

normal.en: The family runs literacy, illiteracy, literature, literal, literary.
normal.cn: 同族包括「读写能力」「文盲状态」「文学」「字面的」「文学的」。

normal.en: The noun use is rare but real, as in counts of literates.
normal.cn: 名词用法少见但真实存在，如统计识字者人数。

abstract.en: Picture a person carrying a bag of letters that opens every official door.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人背着一袋字母，能打开每一扇公务的门。

abstract.en: Picture glasses that turn a page of marks into sentences.
abstract.cn: 想象一副眼镜，把满页符号变成句子。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp kept lit at the same desk for fifty years.
abstract.cn: 想象同一张书桌上点了五十年的灯。

examples.en: A literate population reads instructions and changes behaviour faster.
examples.cn: 识字的人口能更快读懂说明并改变行为。

examples.en: She was literate in three languages before she left school.
examples.cn: 她离开学校前已能用三种语言读写。

examples.en: Any computer-literate volunteer can update the parish register.
examples.cn: 任何会用电脑的志愿者都能更新教区登记册。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「里特瑞特」——里面特别认得那些小字，就是识字的。

root: 拉丁 littera「字母」加表「具有」的形容词后缀构成 litteratus「写有字母的、有学问的」，十五世纪进入英语，后扩展指任何能读写的人。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the plain ability to read through cultivation, practical paperwork, computers, specialist fields and style, until the adjective finally names the people themselves.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从最基本的读写能力出发，经过教养、日常文书、电脑、专业领域与文风，最后用这个形容词直接指人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand tracing lines of print on a page beside a stack of worn books.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手在页面上顺着印刷字行移动，旁边是一摞翻旧的书。

branches.en: THE BASE: the plain ability to read and write comes first.
branches.cn: 基底：能读能写这一朴素能力排在最前。

branches.en: BOOKS AND BEARERS: reading widely shades into cultivation, and the adjective can name the reader.
branches.cn: 书与读书人：广泛阅读渐成教养，而这个形容词也能直接指读者。

branches.en: PAPERWORK: forms and instructions set a practical threshold for the word.
branches.cn: 文书：表格与说明为这个词设下实用门槛。

branches.en: TOOLS AND FIELDS: screens and specialties each have letters of their own.
branches.cn: 工具与领域：屏幕与专业各自拥有自己的「字母」。

branches.en: STYLE AND SOCIETY: polished prose and a reading public are the word written large.
branches.cn: 文风与社会：打磨过的文字与读书的公众，是这个词的放大形态。

intro.en: The word is a Latin adjective carried into English, built from a noun for a letter and a suffix meaning 'provided with'.
intro.cn: 这是一个直接借入英语的拉丁形容词，由表「字母」的名词与表「被赋予」的后缀构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin littera supplied letter, literature and literal, while the adjective litteratus supplied literate and, with a prefix of denial, illiterate.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 littera 衍生出「字母」「文学」与「字面的」，形容词 litteratus 衍生出「识字的」，加上否定前缀则成「不识字的」。

items.example: The noun names the unit a reader must first master.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指读者必须首先掌握的单位。

items.example: The ending turns a possession into a description of a person.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把「拥有某物」变成对人的描述。

items.meaning: provided with letters, able to read
items.example: The witness was literate and signed her own name.
items.exampleCN: 这名证人识字，自己签了名。

items.meaning: the state of being able to read
items.example: Literacy rose sharply after the new school opened.
items.exampleCN: 新学校开办后识字率迅速上升。

items.example: The notice was rewritten for illiterate readers.
items.exampleCN: 这则通知为不识字者重写了一遍。

items.meaning: a sign for a speech sound; a written message
items.example: She wrote the letter in one sitting.
items.exampleCN: 她一口气写完了这封信。

items.example: The magazine reviews literary fiction.
items.exampleCN: 这本杂志评论文学小说。

items.example: The old phrase 'a man of letters' still survives.
items.exampleCN: 「文人」这一旧称仍然存在。

definition_zh: 文盲状态；不识字；（某一领域的）基本无知
definition_en: the inability to read and write, or a lack of the basic knowledge needed in a particular field
core_image: 一张贴在诊所墙上的通知，字行密密麻麻，一个人站在前面反复打量却无法读出内容
scene: 诊所墙上贴着一张密密麻麻的通知，一位老人站在前面反复打量，最后转身问护士。Illiteracy kept him from reading the dosage on the label himself.
sceneCN: 这里指「不识字的状态」（第 1 个义项：缺乏读写能力）；句意为他因不识字，无法自己读出标签上的用量说明。可辨识物件：通知、字行、老人、标签。

pos.zh: 文盲状态；不识字（通常不可数）

senses.title: Inability to read and write
senses.definition: the condition of being unable to read or write a short simple text
senses.definitionCN: 无法读懂或写出简短浅近文字的状态
senses.example: Illiteracy closed doors that a signature would have opened.
senses.exampleCN: 不识字关上了那些本可由一个签名打开的门。
senses.why: the noun is the negative twin of literacy, so its core is the plain absence of letters.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词是「读写能力」的否定孪生词，其核心就是字母的缺席。

senses.title: The measured rate in a population
senses.definition: the share of a population that cannot read, treated as a figure for reports
senses.definitionCN: 不能读写者在人口中的比例，被当作报告用的数字
senses.example: Illiteracy fell by a third in the decade after the campaign.
senses.exampleCN: 扫盲运动之后的十年里，文盲比例下降了三分之一。
senses.why: governments needed a number to track, so the condition became a statistic under the same name.
senses.whyCN: 政府需要一个可追踪的数字，于是这种状态以同一名称变成统计量。

senses.title: Functional illiteracy
senses.titleCN: 能认字却读不懂日常文书
senses.definition: the state of having some schooling yet being unable to use print in daily life
senses.definitionCN: 虽上过学，却无法在日常生活中实际运用文字的状态
senses.example: Functional illiteracy hides behind a school certificate.
senses.exampleCN: 实用性文盲常常藏在毕业证后面。
senses.why: the word widened from absence of letters to inability to use them, which is harder to see.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从「不认识字母」扩展到「不会使用文字」，后者更难察觉。

senses.title: Digital illiteracy
senses.definition: the lack of basic competence with computers and online services
senses.definitionCN: 缺乏使用计算机与网络服务的基本能力
senses.example: Digital illiteracy excludes people from services that moved online.
senses.exampleCN: 数字文盲使一些人被排除在已搬到线上的服务之外。
senses.why: screens introduced a new set of signs, and the old negative noun was reused for them.
senses.whyCN: 屏幕带来一套新的符号，这个旧的否定名词因此被用于其上。

senses.title: Scientific or numerical illiteracy
senses.definition: the lack of the basic ideas needed to judge scientific or quantitative claims
senses.definitionCN: 缺乏判断科学或数量主张所需的基本概念
senses.example: Scientific illiteracy makes a misleading chart hard to challenge.
senses.exampleCN: 科学盲使人难以质疑一张误导性的图表。
senses.why: a field's basic vocabulary is the alphabet one must know, so its absence takes the same name.
senses.whyCN: 某领域的基本词汇就是必须认识的字母，其缺席因此沿用同一名称。

senses.title: Illiteracy as a policy problem
senses.titleCN: 作为公共政策议题的文盲现象
senses.definition: the condition viewed as a social problem that states try to measure and reduce
senses.definitionCN: 被国家试图测量并减少的社会问题
senses.example: The ministry treated illiteracy as an obstacle to economic growth.
senses.exampleCN: 该部把文盲问题视为经济增长的障碍。
senses.why: once the condition is counted, it also becomes something to be governed.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这种状态被计数，它也就成了治理对象。

senses.title: Illiteracy in a region or group
senses.titleCN: 某地区或群体的文盲状况
senses.definition: the extent of the condition among a named population, such as rural women
senses.definitionCN: 在某一特定人群（如农村妇女）中的普遍程度
senses.example: Illiteracy among older women remained the highest in the country.
senses.exampleCN: 年长女性的文盲程度仍是全国最高。
senses.why: once counted, the condition can be compared across groups, and the name travels with the comparison.
senses.whyCN: 一旦被计数，这种状态便可在群体间比较，名称也随之进入比较。

senses.title: Ignorance of a field's basic codes
senses.titleCN: 对某领域基本规则的无知（引申义）
senses.definition: a figurative lack of the basic vocabulary needed to take part in a field
senses.definitionCN: 比喻性地缺乏参与某一领域所需的基本词汇
senses.example: Economic illiteracy made the debate impossible to follow.
senses.exampleCN: 经济盲使这场辩论根本无法跟上。
senses.why: the metaphor is complete once 'letters' means any system of signs a participant must read.
senses.whyCN: 当「字母」泛指参与者必须读懂的任一符号系统时，这个比喻就完整了。

intro.en: Illiteracy is the negative noun matching literacy, built on Latin illitteratus 'unlettered', itself in- 'not' plus litteratus 'lettered'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个词是与「读写能力」相配的否定名词，建于拉丁 illitteratus「不识字的」之上，后者由否定前缀加 litteratus「写有字母的」构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Littera meant a letter of the alphabet, and in the plural writings or a letter. Its deeper origin is not established.
items.cn: littera 指字母，复数指著作或书信。其更深来源未获证明。

items.en: Litteratus 'lettered, learned' was formed with an ending meaning 'provided with'.
items.cn: litteratus「写有字母的、有学问的」由表「带有」的词尾构成。

items.en: The negating prefix in- assimilated to the following consonant, giving illitteratus 'unlettered, unlearned'.
items.cn: 否定前缀因后接辅音而同化，形成 illitteratus「不识字的、无学问的」。

items.en: English formed the noun in the seventeenth century, when schooling and printing made the lack of letters a visible social fact.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪构成这个名词，当时学校教育与印刷使「不识字」成为显见的社会事实。

items.en: From the nineteenth century the word also named a rate to be counted, and from the late twentieth it was extended to digital and scientific fields.
items.cn: 从十九世纪起，这个词也指可计数的比率；二十世纪后期又扩展到数字与科学领域。

items.en: Source uncertain: the pre-Latin origin of the letter-word is unknown, and the earliest printed use of the English noun is not precisely dated.
items.cn: 来源不确定：那个表「字母」的词在拉丁语之前的来源不明，这个英语名词最早的印刷书证年代亦不确切。

note.en: Group one holds forms from the same root that differ only in endings; group two holds words naming a lack of knowledge.
note.cn: 第一组是同根、只差词尾的词形；第二组是表示知识缺乏的词。

entries.definition: Describes someone unable to read, or names such a person; the noun names the condition.
entries.definitionCN: 描述不能读写的某人，或指这样的人；名词则指这种状态。

entries.definition: The ability to read and write; the two nouns differ only by a prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 指读写能力；两个名词只差一个前缀。

entries.definition: Means 'following the exact words' and has no negative force at all.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「照字面的」，完全没有否定含义。

entries.definition: Able to read and write; it is the exact opposite of the adjective form.
entries.definitionCN: 指能读写，与形容词形式正好相反。

entries.definition: A general lack of knowledge; illiteracy is the specific lack of reading and writing.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指缺乏知识；文盲特指缺乏读写能力。

entries.definition: The lack of basic competence with numbers, coined as the counterpart of numeracy.
entries.definitionCN: 指缺乏数字基本能力，是仿「数字能力」造出的反面词。

entries.definition: An older literary word for uneducated; it is close but belongs to formal prose.
entries.definitionCN: 较古雅的说法，指未受教育，意思接近但属正式书面语。

entries.definition: Having only fragmentary reading and writing; it sits between the two poles.
entries.definitionCN: 指读写能力零碎，处于两极之间。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real related words, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实相关词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The word is literacy wearing a prefix of denial, so the pair is learned together.
normal.cn: 这个词就是戴上否定前缀的「读写能力」，两个词宜成对记。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the modern fields: digital illiteracy, scientific illiteracy.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出现代领域：数字文盲、科学盲。

normal.en: The condition is also a number, which is why the phrase illiteracy rate exists.
normal.cn: 这种状态也会变成数字，因此有「文盲率」这一说法。

normal.en: The family runs illiterate, literacy, literate, semiliterate.
normal.cn: 同族包括「不识字的」「读写能力」「识字的」「半文盲的」。

normal.en: Functional illiteracy is the hidden kind: a certificate without usable skills.
normal.cn: 实用性文盲是隐藏的一类：有证书，却没有可用技能。

abstract.en: Picture a notice whose lines turn into a locked door.
abstract.cn: 想象一张通知，上面的字行变成一扇锁住的门。

abstract.en: Picture a map with no names, so every road looks the same.
abstract.cn: 想象一张没有地名的地图，每条路看起来都一样。

abstract.en: Picture a key that exists but cannot be found when the door is closing.
abstract.cn: 想象一把钥匙确实存在，却在门要关时找不到。

examples.en: Illiteracy among rural women fell sharply once village classes opened.
examples.cn: 乡村夜校开办后，农村女性的文盲状况迅速下降。

examples.en: Functional illiteracy can survive years of schooling.
examples.cn: 实用性文盲可以在多年学校教育之后依然存在。

examples.en: Scientific illiteracy leaves people unable to judge a risk for themselves.
examples.cn: 科学盲使人无法自行判断风险。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一里特乐西」——一个字母都认不得，里外都乐不起来，这就是文盲状态。

root: 拉丁 littera「字母」加表「带有」的词尾成 litteratus「识字的」，再加否定前缀构成 illitteratus「不识字的」；英语十七世纪由此构成 illiteracy。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all describe an absence: letters, then usable print, then the tools of a screen age, then the codes of science and of whole fields, until the word finally names any basic ignorance a society decides to count.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在描述一种缺席：先是字母，再是可用的文字，然后是屏幕时代的工具，接着是科学与各领域的规则，最后指社会决定加以计数的任何基本无知。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dense notice on a wall that refuses to become words.
core.cn: 核心意象：墙上密密麻麻的通知，始终不肯变成可读的词。

branches.en: THE BASE ABSENCE: not knowing letters is the oldest and plainest layer.
branches.cn: 基底缺席：不认识字母是最古老也最朴素的一层。

branches.en: COUNTED AND GOVERNED: once measured, the condition becomes a target for policy.
branches.cn: 被计数与被治理：一旦被测量，这种状态就成为政策目标。

branches.en: PRINT WITHOUT USE: schooling can leave people unable to handle real paperwork.
branches.cn: 有字却无用：学校教育可能仍留下不会处理实际文书的人。

branches.en: NEW CODES: screens and scientific claims each demand a literacy of their own.
branches.cn: 新密码：屏幕与科学主张各自要求一套自己的素养。

branches.en: WHO AND WHERE: the condition is unevenly spread, and it can be figurative as well.
branches.cn: 谁与何处：这种状态分布不均，也可作比喻用法。

intro.en: The word is the negative member of a small family built on a Latin root for a letter.
intro.cn: 这个词是建在拉丁语表「字母」词根上的一个小词族中的否定成员。

latinIntro.en: Latin littera gives letter, literature and literal; litteratus gives literate, and with a negating prefix it gives illitteratus.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 littera 衍生出「字母」「文学」与「字面的」；litteratus 衍生出「识字的」，加否定前缀则成 illitteratus。

items.example: The prefix assimilates to the next sound, which is why it appears as il-.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀会与后一个音同化，写作同化后的形式。

items.example: The root names the smallest unit of print.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根指印刷文字的最小单位。

items.example: The adjective describes a person furnished with letters.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词描述一个「带着字母」的人。

items.example: The negative form entered English through learned Latin.
items.exampleCN: 否定形式经学术拉丁语进入英语。

items.example: The label was once used for anyone outside formal schooling.
items.exampleCN: 这个标签曾用于任何未受正规教育的人。

items.example: Illiteracy was treated as a national problem.
items.exampleCN: 文盲被当作一项国家问题。

items.meaning: the ability to read and write
items.example: Literacy programs were funded by the province.
items.exampleCN: 识字项目由省里拨款。

items.example: Semiliterate readers need simpler forms.
items.exampleCN: 半文盲读者需要更简单的表格。

definition_zh: 识字率；识字人口比例（通常以某年龄段能读写人数所占百分比表示）
definition_en: the percentage of a population, usually within a given age group, that can read and write
core_image: 一张摊开的国家统计表，纵横格子里填满百分比，旁边一支红笔把某一行圈了出来
scene: 统计局的长桌上摊着一份国别数据表，格子里的百分比排成一片。The literacy rate for young women doubled in twenty years.
sceneCN: 这里指「能读写人口所占的百分比」（第 1 个义项：衡量识字普及程度的比例指标）；句意为青年女性的识字率在二十年内翻了一番。可辨识物件：数据表、百分比、红笔、长桌。

senses.title: The share of adults who can read
senses.titleCN: 成年人口中能读写的比例
senses.definition: the percentage of people above a stated age who can read and write a simple text
senses.definitionCN: 超过某一年龄的人口中，能读懂并写出浅近文字的百分比
senses.example: The adult literacy rate in the district passed ninety percent last year.
senses.exampleCN: 去年该区的成人识字率超过了百分之九十。
senses.why: the phrase simply puts a measured ability next to a word for a computed proportion.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语只是把一项被测量的能力，与一个表计算比例的词并置。

senses.title: A rate for the young
senses.titleCN: 特定青年年龄段的识字比例
senses.definition: a figure limited to an age band such as fifteen to twenty-four, used to judge schools
senses.definitionCN: 限定在如十五至二十四岁年龄段、用于评估学校成效的数字
senses.example: The youth literacy rate is the clearest sign of what schooling achieved.
senses.exampleCN: 青年识字率是学校教育成效最清楚的标志。
senses.why: limiting the age band makes the number answer a specific question about recent schooling.
senses.whyCN: 限定年龄段，能让这个数字回答关于近期学校教育的具体问题。

senses.title: A national statistic for reports
senses.titleCN: 用于报告的国家统计数字
senses.definition: an official figure a state reports to international bodies
senses.definitionCN: 国家向国际机构报告的一官方数字
senses.example: Each country submits its literacy rate to the agency every year.
senses.exampleCN: 每个国家每年向该机构提交本国的识字率。
senses.why: a single comparable figure is what international reporting requires, so the phrase became official language.
senses.whyCN: 国际报告需要的正是一个可比较的数字，这个短语因此成为官方语言。

senses.title: A measure of the gender gap
senses.definition: a pair of figures compared between women and men to show inequality
senses.definitionCN: 把女性与男性数字并列比较以显示不平等的指标
