senses.example: The gender gap in the literacy rate narrowed over two decades.
senses.exampleCN: 识字率中的性别差距在二十年间缩小了。
senses.why: a single rate can be split by sex, and the comparison is what makes inequality visible.
senses.whyCN: 同一个比率可以按性别拆分，而正是这种比较让不平等变得可见。

senses.title: A way to compare regions
senses.titleCN: 用于比较地区差异的尺度
senses.definition: a single number that lets provinces, cities or districts be ranked against each other
senses.definitionCN: 用一个数字让各省、市或区相互比较排序
senses.example: The literacy rate in the mountain counties lagged behind the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 山区各县的识字率落后于沿海。
senses.why: one figure can be set beside another, which turns a description into a ranking.
senses.whyCN: 一个数字能与另一个并排放置，于是描述变成了排序。

senses.title: A development indicator
senses.definition: one of the figures used to track progress in education and poverty reduction
senses.definitionCN: 用于追踪教育与减贫进展的数字之一
senses.example: Donors watched the literacy rate as one sign of reform.
senses.exampleCN: 捐助方把识字率作为改革迹象之一来观察。
senses.why: aid decisions needed a small set of numbers, and this one entered the standard list.
senses.whyCN: 援助决策需要一小组数字，而这个数字进入了标准清单。

senses.title: A census-derived figure
senses.titleCN: 由人口普查得出的数字
senses.definition: a number produced by asking people in a census whether they can read
senses.definitionCN: 通过普查询问人们能否读写而得出的数字
senses.example: Census data put the literacy rate slightly above the survey estimate.
senses.exampleCN: 普查数据使识字率略高于抽样调查的估计。
senses.why: the number has to come from somewhere, and a census is the largest source that asks everyone.
senses.whyCN: 这个数字必须有来源，而普查是询问所有人的最大来源。

senses.title: A policy target
senses.definition: a level that a government or agency commits itself to reach by a stated date
senses.definitionCN: 政府或机构承诺在指定日期前达到的水平
senses.example: The plan set a literacy rate target of ninety-five percent by the year two thousand.
senses.exampleCN: 该计划把二零零零年前的识字率目标定为百分之九十五。
senses.why: a measured figure becomes a target as soon as a government promises to move it.
senses.whyCN: 一旦政府承诺推动这个数字，测量值就成了目标。

intro.en: Literacy rate joins literacy, from Latin littera 'letter', and rate, from Latin rata pars 'a fixed portion' and reri 'to reckon'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个短语由表「读写能力」与表「比率」的两个名词组合：前者出自拉丁 littera「字母」，后者出自拉丁 rata pars「定额部分」与 reri「计算」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Littera meant a letter of the alphabet; with the adjective litteratus it gave the modern word for being able to read.
items.cn: littera 指字母；与形容词 litteratus 一起，构成现代表「能读写」的词。

items.en: Rata pars meant 'a reckoned or fixed portion', from the participle of reri 'to reckon, think'.
items.cn: rata pars 意为「计算过的、定额的部分」，出自 reri「计算、思考」的分词。

items.en: English rate, borrowed through French, first named a fixed charge or proportion and later any measured ratio.
items.cn: 英语经法语借入「比率」一词，先指固定费用或比例，后指任何被测量的比率。

items.en: The phrase appeared with mass statistics in the twentieth century, when states needed one number for reading ability.
items.cn: 这个短语随二十世纪的大众统计出现，当时国家需要用一个数字表示读写能力。

items.en: International agencies standardized age bands and definitions, making the phrase a comparable indicator.
items.cn: 国际机构统一了年龄段与定义，使这个短语成为可比较的指标。

items.en: Source uncertain: the pre-Latin origin of the letter-word is unknown, and the first use of the exact phrase in an official report is not dated with certainty.
items.cn: 来源不确定：那个表「字母」的词在拉丁语之前的来源不明，这个确切短语首次出现在官方报告中的时间亦无法确证。

note.en: Group one holds look-alike phrases built from the same two nouns; group two holds other educational proportions that are often mistaken for it.
note.cn: 第一组是由同两个名词构成的形近短语；第二组是常被误当作它的其他教育比例。

entries.definition: The ability itself; the full phrase adds a computed proportion to it.
entries.definitionCN: 指能力本身；完整短语在此基础上加了计算出的比例。

entries.definition: Any measured proportion or charge; it says nothing about reading.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指任何被测量的比例或费率，与读写无关。

entries.definition: The percentage who cannot read; the two figures usually sum to the whole population.
entries.definitionCN: 指不能读写的百分比，两个数字通常合成全体人口。

entries.definition: How well people read rather than what share can read, so it is a quality measure.
entries.definitionCN: 指人们读得多好，而非能读的人占多少，属质量尺度。

entries.definition: The share of children registered in school; being enrolled does not prove being literate.
entries.definitionCN: 指注册入学的儿童比例；入学并不等于识字。

entries.definition: The share who finish a level of schooling; it measures persistence, not reading.
entries.definitionCN: 指完成某一学段的比例，衡量的是坚持度而非阅读能力。

entries.definition: The comparable percentage for basic number skills, built on the same pattern.
entries.definitionCN: 指基本数字能力的对应百分比，按同一模式构成。

entries.definition: A composite score mixing years of school and qualifications, unlike the single figure of the phrase.
entries.definitionCN: 指混合了受教育年限与学历的综合得分，不同于该短语的单一数字。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real related words, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实相关词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Half the phrase is an ability and half is a computed proportion, so it always needs a population behind it.
normal.cn: 短语一半是能力，一半是算出的比例，因此它背后总要有一个人群。

normal.en: Fixed phrases attach an age band: adult literacy rate, youth literacy rate.
normal.cn: 固定搭配加上年龄段：成人识字率、青年识字率。

normal.en: The complement is the illiteracy rate, and the two usually add up to the whole.
normal.cn: 它的互补项是文盲率，两者通常加成全体的整体。

normal.en: The second noun is the same one used in interest rate and birth rate.
normal.cn: 第二个名词也用于利率与出生率。

normal.en: The family runs literacy, literate, illiteracy, enrollment rate, completion rate.
normal.cn: 同族包括「读写能力」「识字的」「文盲状态」「入学率」「完成率」。

abstract.en: Picture a long table of percentages with one row circled in red.
abstract.cn: 想象一张满是百分比的长表，其中一行被红笔圈出。

abstract.en: Picture a hundred people in a hall, and a hand counting those who can sign their names.
abstract.cn: 想象大厅里有一百人，一只手在数能签自己名字的人。

abstract.en: Picture two staircases side by side, one for women and one for men, measured at the same step.
abstract.cn: 想象并排的两道楼梯，一道为女性、一道为男性，在同一级台阶上测量。

examples.en: The national literacy rate rose from sixty to eighty percent in a generation.
examples.cn: 全国识字率在一代人之内从六成升到八成。

examples.en: Agencies compare literacy rates only when the age bands match.
examples.cn: 只有当年龄段一致时，各机构才会比较识字率。

examples.en: The province set a literacy rate target for rural women.
examples.cn: 该省为农村女性设定了识字率目标。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「里特乐西」加「瑞特」——认得字的人按比例排成一列，就是识字率。

root: literacy 出自拉丁 littera「字母」及其形容词 litteratus「识字的」；rate 经法语出自拉丁 rata pars「定额部分」与 reri「计算」，本指固定比例，后泛指被测量的比率。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all turn one ability into a number: a share of adults, a band of youth, a national report, a gender comparison, a regional ranking, a development indicator, a census product and finally a target to reach.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都把这同一种能力变成一个数字：成人比例、青年年龄段、国家报告、性别比较、地区排序、发展指标、普查产物，最后是一个要达成的目标。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wide table of percentages with one row circled in red.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张铺开的百分比大表，其中一行被红笔圈出。

branches.en: THE FIRST NUMBER: the share of adults who can read is the standard form.
branches.cn: 第一个数字：能读写的成人比例是标准形态。

branches.en: AGE BANDS: narrowing the figure to the young shows what schools achieved.
branches.cn: 年龄段：把数字收窄到青年，可看出学校的成效。

branches.en: REPORTED AND COUNTED: official submissions and census returns feed the figure.
branches.cn: 上报与计数：官方提交与普查回报为这个数字提供数据。

branches.en: COMPARISONS: the same number ranks men against women and one region against another.
branches.cn: 比较：同一个数字可把男女、把一个地区与另一个地区排出高低。

branches.en: FROM SIGN TO GOAL: a development indicator also becomes a level to reach by a date.
branches.cn: 从迹象到目标：发展指标也会变成须在某日期前达到的水平。

intro.en: The phrase is two nouns, one for an ability and one for a computed proportion, each with a productive Latin core.
intro.cn: 这个短语由两个名词构成，一个表能力，一个表计算出的比例，各自都有一个能产的拉丁内核。

latinIntro.en: Latin littera and litteratus supply the reading family; Latin rata and reri supply the family of reckoning and ratio.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 littera 与 litteratus 提供「读写」一族；拉丁 rata 与 reri 提供「计算与比率」一族。

items.example: The root names what a reader must first learn.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根指读者最先要学的东西。

items.meaning: the ability to read and write
items.example: Literacy is measured, not assumed.
items.exampleCN: 读写能力是被测量的，而非假定的。

items.example: The rate is stated as a percentage.
items.exampleCN: 这个比率以百分比表示。

items.example: The ratio of readers to non-readers was two to one.
items.exampleCN: 能读者与不能读者之比为二比一。

items.structure: Latin ratio carried into French and English
items.example: The same root that counts also thinks.
items.exampleCN: 同一个表示「计算」的词根也用于「思考」。

items.example: A literate adult counts once in the numerator.
items.exampleCN: 一个识字成人计入分子一次。

items.example: The two rates usually sum to the whole.
items.exampleCN: 两个比率通常加成全体的整体。

items.example: Enrollment can rise before literacy does.
items.exampleCN: 入学率可能先于识字率上升。

latinEntries.structure: rata, ratae (f., first declension; as in rata pars)
reri, ratus sum (verb, deponent, second conjugation)

definition_zh: 语言；言语；（某一领域的）表达方式；计算机语言
definition_en: a system of spoken or written signs used for communication, or a particular style or code of expression
core_image: 一张围着许多人的旧木桌，桌上摊着写满不同文字的纸页，几个人正用手势和声音相互回应
scene: 旧木桌旁围坐着来自几座村镇的人，桌上摊着写满不同文字的纸页。Language was the only tool they had in common that afternoon.
sceneCN: 这里指「用于交流的声音与符号系统」（第 1 个义项：人类交流的整体系统）；句意为那天下午，语言是他们唯一共同拥有的工具。可辨识物件：旧木桌、纸页、不同文字、手势。

pos.zh: 语言；言语；表达方式（可数与不可数两用）

senses.title: The human system of communication
senses.titleCN: 人类用于交流的符号系统
senses.definition: the shared system of sounds, words and grammar by which people communicate
senses.definitionCN: 人们借以交流的声音、词汇与语法的共享系统
senses.example: Language is learned in company, not from a dictionary alone.
senses.exampleCN: 语言是在与人相处中学到的，而不是只靠词典。
senses.why: the word came from the Latin name for the tongue, so the oldest image is the organ that produces speech.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自拉丁语对「舌头」的称呼，因此最古老的画面是发出言语的器官。

senses.title: A particular named tongue
senses.definition: a specific system such as Chinese, Arabic or Swahili, counted as one item
senses.definitionCN: 如汉语、阿拉伯语或斯瓦希里语等具体系统，可作为一个单位计数
senses.example: She speaks four languages and reads two more.
senses.exampleCN: 她会说四种语言，还能读另外两种。
senses.why: once the general capacity was recognized, each separate system needed the same name.
senses.whyCN: 当整体能力被认出之后，每一个独立的系统也需要同一个名称。

senses.title: Speech as it is actually used
senses.definition: the spoken words of a person or group on a given occasion, as opposed to writing
senses.definitionCN: 某人或某群体在某一场合说出的具体话语，与书面语相对
senses.example: His language in the meeting was far plainer than his letters.
senses.exampleCN: 他在会上说的话比他的书信朴素得多。
senses.why: the tongue is the instrument of speech, so the word also names the spoken output itself.
senses.whyCN: 舌头是说话的器官，因此这个词也指说出来的产物。

senses.title: The style and wording of a text
senses.definition: the choice of words and sentence patterns that gives a text its tone
senses.definitionCN: 使文本形成某种语气的用词与句式选择
senses.example: The language of the report was careful but cold.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告的措辞谨慎而冷淡。
senses.why: a text's manner of speech can be described with the same word used for a nation's tongue.
senses.whyCN: 一个文本的说话方式，可以用描述民族语言的同一个词来指称。

senses.title: The vocabulary of a special field
senses.titleCN: 某一专业的行话与术语
senses.definition: the technical words and conventions used by a profession or subject
senses.definitionCN: 某职业或学科使用的术语与惯例
senses.example: Legal language keeps ordinary readers at a distance.
senses.exampleCN: 法律行话把普通读者挡在门外。
senses.why: a profession speaks its own tongue, so its terms are called a language.
senses.whyCN: 一个职业说自己的话，因此其术语被称作一种语言。

senses.title: A code for machines
senses.definition: a formal set of instructions that a computer can process
senses.definitionCN: 计算机可以处理的一套形式化指令
senses.example: The course teaches one programming language at a time.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课一次只教一种编程语言。
senses.why: the word was extended to any rule-governed code, including one no human speaks.
senses.whyCN: 这个词被扩展到任何有规则的代码，包括没有人说的那种。

senses.title: Non-verbal signals
senses.definition: meaning carried by gesture, posture or tone rather than words
senses.definitionCN: 由手势、姿态或语气而非词语承载的意义
senses.example: Her body language said more than her answer.
senses.exampleCN: 她的肢体语言比回答说明了更多。
senses.why: meaning is carried without the tongue at all, and the word follows the meaning.
senses.whyCN: 意义完全不经舌头而传递，词也跟着意义走。

senses.title: The human capacity for speech
senses.titleCN: 人类拥有语言的天赋能力
senses.definition: the general human ability to acquire and use a grammar, studied as a faculty
senses.definitionCN: 人类习得并使用语法的总体能力，被当作一种官能来研究
senses.example: Language separates human communication from simple signalling.
senses.exampleCN: 语言使人类交流区别于简单的信号传递。
senses.why: the most abstract sense returns to the original faculty that makes every other sense possible.
senses.whyCN: 最抽象的义项回到那项使其他所有义项成为可能的原初官能。

intro.en: Language comes from Old French langage, from Latin lingua 'tongue, language'. The further origin of lingua is not established. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个词来自古法语 langage，再上溯拉丁 lingua「舌头、语言」。lingua 更早的来源未获证明。年代均为约数。

items.en: Lingua meant both 'tongue' and 'language'. The sense grew from the organ to what the organ produces, a common pattern in many languages.
items.cn: lingua 兼指「舌头」与「语言」。词义从器官转到器官的产物，这在许多语言中都是常见模式。

items.en: The deeper origin of lingua is unsettled. A link sometimes proposed with a verb meaning 'to lick' is a hypothesis, not a demonstrated derivation.
items.cn: lingua 更深的来源没有定论。有人提出它与一个表「舔」的动词有关，那只是假说，并非已证实的派生。

items.en: Old French langage named speech and the way one speaks; English borrowed it in the age of Norman rule.
items.cn: 古法语 langage 指言语及说话方式；英语在诺曼统治时期借入。

items.en: Middle English used the word for a nation's tongue and for a person's manner of speech, both senses surviving today.
items.cn: 中古英语用这个词指一个民族的语言，也指个人的说话方式，两义都留存至今。

items.en: Modern technical life extended the word to formal codes, giving programming languages, and to gesture, giving body language.
items.cn: 现代技术生活把词扩展到形式化代码，产生「编程语言」，也扩展到姿态，产生「肢体语言」。

items.en: Source uncertain: no attested pre-Latin form of lingua is agreed, and the exact route through French is reconstructed from later records.
items.cn: 来源不确定：lingua 在拉丁语之前的形式没有公认书证，经法语传入的确切路径亦由较晚记录构拟。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same root that are often confused; group two holds near neighbours that name communication.
note.cn: 第一组是同根而常被混淆的词；第二组是表示交流的近义词。

entries.definition: Describes what relates to language; it never names the system itself.
entries.definitionCN: 描述与语言有关的性质，本身不指那套系统。

entries.definition: The scientific study of language, not a language and not a person.
entries.definitionCN: 指对语言的科学研究，既不是一种语言，也不是一个人。

entries.definition: A person who studies language, or loosely one who knows several.
entries.definitionCN: 指研究语言的人，或宽泛地指通晓多种语言的人。

entries.definition: An informal word for a foreign language or a jargon; it is playful where language is neutral.
entries.definitionCN: 指外语或行话的口语说法，语气戏谑，而「语言」一词为中性。

entries.definition: The act or occasion of speaking; it covers sound but not writing or the abstract system.
entries.definitionCN: 指说话的行为或场合，覆盖声音，却不含书面语或抽象系统。

entries.definition: An old word for a language, as in the mother tongue; it is close but archaic in most uses.
entries.definitionCN: 指语言的旧说法，如「母语」；意思接近，但多数用法已古旧。

entries.definition: One variety within a language; calling it a language is a political judgement.
entries.definitionCN: 指一种语言内部的变体；称它为「语言」常是政治判断。

entries.definition: Any system of signs with rules, including machines; it lacks the human and social weight of language.
entries.definitionCN: 指任何有规则的符号系统，包括机器；缺少语言的人类与社会分量。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real related words, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实相关词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The root means 'tongue', so the word begins as the body part that makes speech.
normal.cn: 词根意为「舌头」，因此这个词最初就是制造言语的身体部位。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the range: foreign language, body language, programming language.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出范围：外语、肢体语言、编程语言。

normal.en: The adjective, the discipline and the person all come from the same root.
normal.cn: 形容词、学科与人都出自同一词根。

normal.en: The family runs linguistic, linguistics, linguist, multilingual, bilingual.
normal.cn: 同族包括「语言的」「语言学」「语言学家」「多语的」「双语的」。

normal.en: Counting languages uses the plural, speaking in general uses the singular.
normal.cn: 数具体语言用复数，泛指说话能力用单数。

abstract.en: Picture a table where every sheet is written in a different hand.
abstract.cn: 想象一张桌子，每张纸都出自不同的笔迹。

abstract.en: Picture a bridge built from sounds rather than stones.
abstract.cn: 想象一座用声音而非石头搭成的桥。

abstract.en: Picture a key ring that opens a different door for every listener.
abstract.cn: 想象一串钥匙，对每个听者打开不同的一扇门。

examples.en: Language changes faster in cities than in isolated valleys.
examples.cn: 语言在城市里的变化比在封闭山谷中更快。

examples.en: The two communities share a border but not a language.
examples.cn: 这两个社群共享一条边界，却不共享一种语言。

examples.en: Nurses are trained to read the body language of anxious patients.
examples.cn: 护士受过训练，能读懂焦虑病人的肢体语言。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「兰格维吉」——拦住陌生人开口，靠的就是这套声音与符号的系统。

root: 拉丁 lingua「舌头、语言」经古法语 langage 进入英语；词义由器官转向器官的产物。lingua 更深来源不确定，与表「舔」动词的联系仅为假说。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses spread from one organ: the tongue produces speech, speech becomes a named system, that system takes styles and jargons, and the same word is finally lent to machines and to silent gesture.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一个器官铺开：舌头产生言语，言语成为具名的系统，系统又生出风格与行话，最后同一个词被借给机器与无声的姿态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one table, many scripts, and hands answering in gesture and sound.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张桌子、多种文字，人们用手势与声音相互回应。

branches.en: THE CAPACITY: the human faculty and its shared system are the two sides of one coin.
branches.cn: 能力：人类的官能与共享系统是同一枚硬币的两面。

branches.en: COUNTED TONGUES: each separate system can be named and counted.
branches.cn: 可数的语言：每一套独立系统都可被命名与计数。

branches.en: BEYOND WORDS: actual speech and silent gesture both carry meaning.
branches.cn: 超出词语：实际说出的话与无声的姿态都承载意义。

branches.en: TONE OF A TEXT: word choice alone can make writing warm or cold.
branches.cn: 文本的语气：仅靠选词就能让文字变暖或变冷。

branches.en: RULED CODES: a profession's jargon and a machine's instructions are both governed sets.
branches.cn: 有规则的代码：专业行话与机器指令都是受规则支配的集合。

intro.en: The word is a French-shaped noun built on a Latin root meaning 'tongue', and that root also builds the whole linguistic family.
intro.cn: 这个词是经法语成形的名词，建在拉丁语表「舌头」的词根上，这个词根也构成整个「语言」词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin lingua gives language, linguist and linguistics through French and Latin endings; the same root appears in the adjective for 'tongue-shaped'.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 lingua 经法语与拉丁词尾衍生出「语言」「语言学家」与「语言学」；同一词根也出现在表「舌形」的形容词里。

items.meaning: the organ of speech, and speech itself
items.example: The root already carries both the body part and its product.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根已同时带着器官与其产物。

items.example: Language is older than any dictionary.
items.exampleCN: 语言比任何词典都古老。

items.example: The linguist recorded the last speakers.
items.exampleCN: 这位语言学家记录了最后的说话者。

items.example: Linguistic evidence dated the text.
items.exampleCN: 语言证据为这份文本定了年代。

items.example: Linguistics became a university subject.
items.exampleCN: 语言学成为一门大学学科。

items.example: Bilingual signs appeared at the airport.
items.exampleCN: 机场出现了双语标识。

items.example: The city is proudly multilingual.
items.exampleCN: 这座城市以多语并存为荣。

items.example: The manual is full of technical lingo.
items.exampleCN: 这本手册满是技术行话。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 双舌的；使用两种语言的

definition_zh: 语言的；语言学的；与语言运用有关的
definition_en: relating to language or to the scientific study of language
core_image: 一页写满分句与箭头的手稿，句子之间用细线连起，页边标着几个小号数
scene: 书桌上摊着一页写满分句与箭头的手稿，句子之间用细线相连。The editors examined linguistic clues before they dated the manuscript.
sceneCN: 这里指「与语言特征有关的」（第 1 个义项：涉及语言本身的）；句意为编者在为手稿定年之前，先检查了语言线索。可辨识物件：手稿、分句、箭头、细线。

senses.title: Relating to language itself
senses.definition: concerning the sounds, words and grammar of a language
senses.definitionCN: 涉及一种语言的声音、词汇与语法
senses.example: Linguistic change is usually gradual rather than sudden.
senses.exampleCN: 语言变化通常是渐进的，而不是突然的。
senses.why: the adjective simply attaches the Latin word for language to any feature of it.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词只是把拉丁语表「语言」的词挂到语言的任何特征上。

senses.title: Relating to the discipline of linguistics
senses.definition: belonging to the scientific study of language as a field
senses.definitionCN: 属于把语言作为研究对象的科学领域
senses.example: The paper appeared in a linguistic journal, not a literary one.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇论文发表在一份语言学刊物上，而非文学刊物。
senses.why: the noun for the field and the adjective for it differ by one ending, so the same description covers both language and its study.
senses.whyCN: 学科名词与它的形容词只差一个词尾，因此同一描述既覆盖语言，也覆盖对语言的研究。

senses.title: Inner knowledge of grammar
senses.titleCN: 说话者内在的语法知识
senses.definition: describing the tacit knowledge a speaker has of the rules of a language
senses.definitionCN: 描述说话者对某一语言规则的默会知识
senses.example: Children's linguistic competence grows faster than their vocabulary lists suggest.
senses.exampleCN: 儿童的语言能力增长得比词汇表所显示的更快。
senses.why: the discipline drew a line between what a speaker knows and what a speaker does.
senses.whyCN: 这门学科在「说话者知道什么」与「说话者做什么」之间划了一条线。

senses.title: A minority defined by its tongue
senses.titleCN: 以语言划分的少数群体
senses.definition: naming a community distinguished by the language it speaks
senses.definitionCN: 指以所说语言而区分出来的群体
senses.example: Linguistic minorities won the right to local schooling.
senses.exampleCN: 语言少数群体争取到了地方办学的权利。
senses.why: a community can be marked out by the tongue it uses, and the adjective follows that marker.
senses.whyCN: 一个群体可以由其所用语言标记出来，形容词便跟着这个标记走。

senses.title: Variety across languages
senses.definition: describing the range of different languages and their features
senses.definitionCN: 描述不同语言及其特征的分布范围
senses.example: The region's linguistic diversity is greater than its biological diversity.
senses.exampleCN: 该地区的语言多样性超过它的生物多样性。
senses.why: counting different tongues turns the adjective into a word about range.
senses.whyCN: 把不同语言计数，就让这个形容词变成关于「范围」的词。

senses.title: Classification by structure
senses.definition: used of the comparison and classification of language structures
senses.definitionCN: 用于语言结构的比较与分类
senses.example: Linguistic typology groups languages by how they build sentences.
senses.exampleCN: 语言类型学按造句方式给语言分组。
senses.why: to compare structures is to classify them, and classification is another face of the adjective.
senses.whyCN: 比较结构就是给结构分类，而分类是这个形容词的另一副面孔。

senses.title: A barrier caused by language
senses.definition: describing an obstacle that arises because people do not share a tongue
senses.definitionCN: 描述因人们不共用一种语言而产生的障碍
senses.example: The linguistic barrier mattered more than the border itself.
senses.exampleCN: 语言障碍比边界本身更要紧。
senses.why: where tongues differ, communication can fail, so the adjective also names an obstacle.
senses.whyCN: 语言不同处，交流可能失败，因此这个形容词也指障碍。

senses.title: Wording used as evidence
senses.definition: describing features of wording that can identify or date a text
senses.definitionCN: 描述可用于识别或为文本定年的措辞特征
senses.example: Linguistic evidence placed the letter in the late sixteenth century.
senses.exampleCN: 语言证据把这封信定在十六世纪后期。
senses.why: wording leaves traces that can be read, so the adjective moves from language to evidence.
senses.whyCN: 措辞留下可读的痕迹，因此这个形容词从语言转到证据。

intro.en: Linguistic is a nineteenth-century adjective built on Latin lingua 'tongue, language' with the ending -isticus, probably through French. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个词是十九世纪形成的形容词，建在拉丁 lingua「舌头、语言」之上，带拉丁形容词词尾，很可能经法语传入。年代均为约数。

items.en: Lingua meant 'tongue' and 'language'; its deeper origin is unsettled and is not demonstrated by any attested older form.
items.cn: lingua 兼指「舌头」与「语言」；其更深来源无定论，也没有任何可证实的更早形式。

items.en: The ending -isticus, taken from Greek, built adjectives meaning 'of or relating to a practice or field'.
items.cn: 这个源自希腊语的词尾构成形容词，意为「属于或关于某实践或领域的」。

items.en: French formed linguistique for the study of language in the early nineteenth century, and English took the adjective soon after.
items.cn: 法语在十九世纪初为语言研究造出相应形容词，英语随后借入。

items.en: As linguistics became a university subject, the adjective came to mean both 'of language' and 'of the discipline'.
items.cn: 随着语言学成为大学学科，这个形容词既指「语言的」，也指「语言学的」。

items.en: The twentieth century added phrases such as linguistic minority and linguistic evidence, extending the adjective into law and history.
items.cn: 二十世纪增加了「语言少数群体」「语言证据」等说法，把这个形容词扩展到法律与历史领域。

items.en: Source uncertain: the pre-Latin origin of the root is unknown, and the exact first English printing of the adjective is not documented.
items.cn: 来源不确定：该词根在拉丁语之前的来源不明，这个形容词最早的英语印刷记录亦无确切文献。

note.en: Group one holds the same-root words that are easily swapped for the adjective; group two holds adjectives describing language matters.
note.cn: 第一组是同根、容易与这个形容词混用的词；第二组是描述语言事务的形容词。

entries.definition: The name of the discipline; the adjective describes something within it.
entries.definitionCN: 指学科名称；形容词则描述该学科之内的事物。

entries.definition: A person who studies language; it is a noun for a doer.
entries.definitionCN: 指研究语言的人，是表施动者的名词。

entries.definition: The system itself; the adjective cannot stand for the system.
entries.definitionCN: 指系统本身；形容词不能替代那个系统。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning 'of the tongue' in anatomy or dentistry, not 'of language'.
entries.definitionCN: 在解剖与牙科中指「舌的」，而非「语言的」。

entries.definition: Relating to words as opposed to actions; it does not refer to grammar or language systems.
entries.definitionCN: 指以词语而非行动表达，不涉及语法或语言系统。

entries.definition: Concerned with meaning rather than structure; it is one part of what linguistic covers.
entries.definitionCN: 关注意义而非结构，是语言研究覆盖的一部分。

entries.definition: Concerned with grammar or with whether a sentence is well formed.
entries.definitionCN: 关注语法或句子是否合式。

entries.definition: Relating to the older study of texts and languages; it is historical where linguistic is general.
entries.definitionCN: 指较旧的文本与语言考据之学，偏历史，而「语言的」更宽泛。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real related words, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实相关词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The adjective carries the same root as the noun for tongue, so it always points back to speech.
normal.cn: 这个形容词与表「舌头」的名词共享词根，因此总指向言语。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show the fields: linguistic diversity, linguistic evidence, linguistic minority.
normal.cn: 固定搭配显示领域：语言多样性、语言证据、语言少数群体。

normal.en: The adverb adds a manner: linguistically speaking.
normal.cn: 副词加上方式：从语言上说。

normal.en: The family runs language, linguist, linguistics, bilingual, multilingual.
normal.cn: 同族包括「语言」「语言学家」「语言学」「双语的」「多语的」。

normal.en: A text marked with arrows between clauses is the picture to keep.
normal.cn: 在分句之间画箭头的那页文本，是要留住的画面。

abstract.en: Picture a fingerprint made of vowels instead of ridges.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚由元音而非纹路组成的指纹。

abstract.en: Picture a map whose borders follow the spread of words.
abstract.cn: 想象一张边界沿着词语传播而画的图。

abstract.en: Picture a fence built between two villages out of untranslated signs.
abstract.cn: 想象两个村子之间用无法翻译的标牌搭成的一道栅栏。

examples.en: Linguistic differences often survive political union by centuries.
examples.cn: 语言差异常常在政治统一之后还延续几个世纪。

examples.en: The court accepted linguistic analysis as evidence of authorship.
examples.cn: 法庭接受语言分析作为作者身份的证据。

examples.en: Linguistic minorities asked for bilingual ballots.
examples.cn: 语言少数群体要求提供双语选票。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「林归斯提克」——林子里归拢来的那套说话规矩，就是语言的。

root: 拉丁 lingua「舌头、语言」加源自希腊语的形容词词尾构成，十九世纪经法语进入英语，指「语言的」，后也指「语言学的」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all attach the adjective to a different object: the language itself, the discipline, the speaker's inner rules, a community, a range of tongues, a classification, a barrier and a piece of evidence.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都把这个形容词挂到不同对象上：语言本身、学科、说话者的内在规则、一个群体、语言的范围、一种分类、一道障碍以及一份证据。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a manuscript page where clauses are linked by thin arrows.
core.cn: 核心意象：一页手稿，分句之间用细箭头相连。

branches.en: THE SIMPLEST LINK: any feature of a language can take the adjective.
branches.cn: 最简单的连接：语言的任何特征都能带这个形容词。

branches.en: THE FIELD: the same adjective also marks work done inside the discipline.
branches.cn: 学科：同一个形容词也标记学科内部的研究。

branches.en: INSIDE THE SPEAKER: tacit grammatical knowledge is a linguistic fact too.
branches.cn: 说话者之内：默会的语法知识同样是语言事实。

branches.en: GROUPS AND RANGES: communities are defined by tongues, and tongues differ widely.
branches.cn: 群体与范围：社群由语言界定，而语言彼此差异很大。

branches.en: ORDER, OBSTACLE, PROOF: structure can be classified, difference can block, and wording can testify.
branches.cn: 秩序、障碍与证据：结构可被分类，差异会成阻碍，而措辞可以提供证明。

intro.en: The word is a Latin-rooted adjective with a Greek-derived ending, so it can be read as root plus ending.
intro.cn: 这是一个带拉丁词根与希腊来源词尾的形容词，可按「词根加词尾」来读。

latinIntro.en: Latin lingua supplies the root; the ending came into Latin from Greek and later built many English adjectives of fields and practices.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 lingua 提供词根；词尾经拉丁语来自希腊语，后来构成许多英语中表领域与实践的形容词。

items.example: The root ties every sense back to speech.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根把每个义项都系回言语。

items.structure: Greek-derived ending via Latin, 'of or relating to'
items.meaning: belonging to a field or practice
items.example: The ending turns a field into a describing word.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把领域变成描述词。

items.example: Language is the object the adjective points to.
items.exampleCN: 语言是这个形容词所指的对象。

items.example: A linguist works on sound, grammar or meaning.
items.exampleCN: 语言研究者研究声音、语法或意义。

items.example: Linguistics has its own methods and journals.
items.exampleCN: 语言学有自己的方法与期刊。

items.example: The two regions are linguistically close.
items.exampleCN: 这两个地区在语言上很接近。

items.example: Bilingual education began in the border counties.
items.exampleCN: 双语教育从边境各县开始。

items.example: A multilingual staff serves the port.
items.exampleCN: 一支多语员工队伍服务这个港口。

definition_zh: 语言学（研究语言的结构、使用与历史的学科）
definition_en: the scientific study of language, including its sounds, structure, meaning, use and history
core_image: 一张铺开的长桌上摆着录音机、音标卡片与写着句法树的黑板照片，四角用镇纸压住
scene: 研究室的桌上摆着录音机、音标卡片与一张句法树的照片，四角都用镇纸压住。Modern linguistics borrows methods from psychology and computer science.
sceneCN: 这里指「研究语言结构、使用与历史的学科」（第 1 个义项：把语言作为科学研究对象的学问）；句意为现代语言学从心理学与计算机科学借用方法。可辨识物件：录音机、音标卡片、句法树、镇纸。

pos.zh: 语言学（作单数；指分支或学派时可用复数）

senses.title: The science of language in general
senses.definition: the systematic study of how languages are structured, learned and used
senses.definitionCN: 对语言如何构成、习得与使用的系统研究
senses.example: Linguistics asks how children acquire grammar without being taught it.
senses.exampleCN: 语言学追问儿童如何在无人教授的情况下习得语法。
senses.why: the name was formed from the adjective for language plus a suffix naming a field of study.
senses.whyCN: 这个名称由表「语言的」形容词加表研究领域的后缀构成。

senses.title: A particular school of theory
senses.definition: one theoretical framework within the field, such as structural or generative linguistics
senses.definitionCN: 该领域内的某一理论框架，如结构主义或生成语法语言学
senses.example: Generative linguistics dominated the department for thirty years.
senses.exampleCN: 生成语法语言学在这个系主导了三十年。
senses.why: a shared framework gives the field a recognisable shape, and each framework takes the field's name.
senses.whyCN: 共享框架给学科一个可辨认的形状，每一个框架都沿用学科之名。

senses.title: A subfield or department
senses.definition: a named branch or organizational unit, such as applied linguistics
senses.definitionCN: 具名的分支或有组织的单位，如应用语言学
senses.example: Applied linguistics sits between teaching and research.
senses.exampleCN: 应用语言学处在教学与研究之间。
senses.why: universities divide the field into named units, and each unit carries the field's name.
senses.whyCN: 大学把学科分成具名单位，每个单位都带着学科之名。

senses.title: The historical study of languages
senses.definition: the branch that traces how sounds, words and forms change over time
senses.definitionCN: 追踪语音、词汇与形式随时间变化的那个分支
senses.example: Historical linguistics can date a split between two dialects.
senses.exampleCN: 历史语言学能为两种方言的分化定年。
senses.why: change over time is one of the field's oldest questions, so the branch keeps the field's name.
senses.whyCN: 随时间变化是这门学科最古老的问题之一，因此该分支保留学科之名。

senses.title: Language in its social setting
senses.titleCN: 社会情境中的语言研究
senses.definition: the branch that studies how class, gender and region shape speech
senses.definitionCN: 研究阶层、性别与地区如何塑造言语的分支
senses.example: Sociolinguistics showed that the same speaker shifts style by audience.
senses.exampleCN: 社会语言学表明，同一个说话者会随听众改变语体。
senses.why: speech varies with company, and that variation is studied under the field's name.
senses.whyCN: 言语随交往对象而变，这种变异也在学科名下被研究。

senses.title: Language handled by machines
senses.titleCN: 由机器处理的语言研究
senses.definition: the branch that builds models and tools for automatic language processing
senses.definitionCN: 建立自动语言处理模型与工具的分支
senses.example: Computational linguistics made the translation tool possible.
senses.exampleCN: 计算语言学使这款翻译工具成为可能。
senses.why: machines need formal models of language, which the field supplies.
senses.whyCN: 机器需要语言的形式模型，而这正是该学科提供的。

senses.title: Linguistic analysis as a method
senses.definition: the use of linguistic techniques to analyse a text, a dispute or a recording
senses.definitionCN: 用语言技术分析文本、争议或录音
senses.example: The lawsuit turned on linguistics as much as on law.
senses.exampleCN: 这起诉讼的胜负，语言学与法律同样关键。
senses.why: the discipline's name is borrowed whenever its methods are applied outside it.
senses.whyCN: 这门学科的方法一旦被用到别处，学科名也随之被借用。

senses.title: The descriptive study of one language
senses.titleCN: 对单一语言的描写研究
senses.definition: the detailed description of a single language's sound system and grammar
senses.definitionCN: 对某一种语言语音系统与语法的细致描写
senses.example: The linguistics of the island's sign language is still barely recorded.
senses.exampleCN: 这座岛屿手语的语言学研究几乎还没有记录。
senses.why: the field can also be narrowed to a single tongue, and the name stays.
senses.whyCN: 学科也可以收窄到单一语言，名称保持不变。

intro.en: Linguistics is the adjective linguistic plus the field-naming ending -s, modelled on French and German terms of the nineteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个词是在形容词「语言的」上加表研究领域的词尾构成，仿照十九世纪的法语与德语说法。年代均为约数。

items.en: Lingua meant 'tongue, language'. Its deeper origin is unsettled, and no older form is attested.
items.cn: lingua 意为「舌头、语言」，其更深来源无定论，也没有更早形式的书证。

items.en: French used a single term for the study of language in the early nineteenth century, and English took both the adjective and the field name from it.
items.cn: 法语在十九世纪初用一个词指语言研究，英语从它借入了形容词与学科名。

items.en: German scholarship also fixed a name for the new science, which helped the English noun settle.
items.cn: 德语学界也为这门新科学定下名称，促成了英语名词的定型。

items.en: English formed the noun in the nineteenth century and made it singular in use, even though it ends like a plural.
items.cn: 英语在十九世纪构成这个名词，尽管词尾形似复数，实际作单数使用。

items.en: The twentieth century multiplied named branches, from sociolinguistics to computational linguistics.
items.cn: 二十世纪不断衍生具名分支，从社会语言学一直到计算语言学。

items.en: Source uncertain: the first fixed use of the English field name is not precisely dated, and the pre-Latin root remains unknown.
items.cn: 来源不确定：这个英语学科名最早的确切使用年代不明，其在拉丁语之前的词根亦未知。

note.en: Group one holds the same-root forms that are always being confused; group two holds neighbouring fields.
note.cn: 第一组是同根而总被混淆的词形；第二组是相邻的学科。

entries.definition: Describes something as relating to language; it is not the name of the field.
entries.definitionCN: 描述某物与语言有关，并非学科名称。

entries.definition: A practitioner of the field, or loosely a speaker of many languages.
entries.definitionCN: 指该领域的从业者，或宽泛地指会说多种语言的人。

entries.definition: The thing the field studies; the discipline and its object are different words.
entries.definitionCN: 指被研究的对象；学科与其对象是两个不同的词。

entries.definition: The historical study of texts and languages; linguistics grew partly out of it.
entries.definitionCN: 指对文本与语言的历史考据，语言学有一部分由它发展而来。

entries.definition: The branch studying speech sounds; it is one part of linguistics.
entries.definitionCN: 研究语音的分支，是语言学的一部分。

entries.definition: The study of how words combine into sentences, a core branch of the field.
entries.definitionCN: 研究词如何组合成句，是该领域的核心分支。

entries.definition: The study of meaning in language, another branch of linguistics.
entries.definitionCN: 研究语言中的意义，是语言学的另一分支。

entries.definition: The rules themselves or a book of them; linguistics studies grammar rather than prescribing it.
entries.definitionCN: 指规则本身或规则书；语言学研究语法而不规定语法。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real related words, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实相关词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The name looks plural but works as a singular, like many names of sciences.
normal.cn: 这个名称形似复数，却作单数用，许多学科名都是如此。

normal.en: Fixed phrases name the branches: applied, historical and computational linguistics.
normal.cn: 固定搭配列出分支：应用语言学、历史语言学、计算语言学。

normal.en: The adjective, the person and the field differ only by their endings.
normal.cn: 形容词、人与学科只差各自的词尾。

normal.en: The family runs linguist, linguistic, sociolinguistics, psycholinguistics.
normal.cn: 同族包括「语言学家」「语言的」「社会语言学」「心理语言学」。

normal.en: A desk with a recorder and a syntax tree is the picture of the discipline at work.
normal.cn: 摆着录音机与句法树的桌子，就是这门学科工作时的画面。

abstract.en: Picture a grammar treated like a living organism under a lens.
abstract.cn: 想象把语法当作镜头下的活体来观察。

abstract.en: Picture a map of sounds rather than of roads.
abstract.cn: 想象一张声音的地图，而不是道路的地图。

abstract.en: Picture a workshop where sentences are taken apart and rebuilt.
abstract.cn: 想象一间工坊，句子被拆开又重新装回。

examples.en: Linguistics turned the study of grammar from prescription into description.
examples.cn: 语言学把语法研究从规定转向描写。

examples.en: She took linguistics because she wanted to understand her own dialect.
examples.cn: 她学语言学，是因为想弄懂自己的方言。

examples.en: Computational linguistics now fills the translation apps people use daily.
examples.cn: 计算语言学如今支撑着人们日常使用的翻译应用。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「林归斯提克斯」——把林子里的说话方式全部归拢、分类、拆开看，就是语言学。

root: 拉丁 lingua「舌头、语言」加希腊来源的形容词词尾，再叠加表研究领域的词尾构成；十九世纪仿法语与德语说法定型，指研究语言的科学。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all name the same science but from different angles: the whole field, a theory, a department, history, society, machines, a borrowed method, and the description of a single tongue.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都指同一门科学，只是角度不同：整个领域、一种理论、一个院系、历史、社会、机器、被借用的方法，以及对单一语言的描写。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a recorder, phonetic cards and a syntax tree pinned under paperweights.
core.cn: 核心意象：录音机、音标卡片与被镇纸压住的句法树。

branches.en: THE WHOLE: the general science of language is the trunk of every other use.
branches.cn: 整体：研究语言的一般科学是其他用法的树干。

branches.en: ORGANIZED FORMS: a theory and a department are the field given a shape.
branches.cn: 有形的组织：理论，院系，是这门领域获得形状的方式。

branches.en: TIME AND COMPANY: languages change across centuries and shift with audience.
branches.cn: 时间与同伴：语言跨越世纪而变，也随听众而变。

branches.en: FROM MACHINES TO ONE TONGUE: the field ranges from automatic processing to a single sign language.
branches.cn: 从机器到单一语言：这门学问既研究自动处理，也描写一种手语。

branches.en: BORROWED METHODS: once the techniques travel, the field's name travels with them.
branches.cn: 被借用的方法：技术一旦外流，学科名也随之而去。

intro.en: The word is an adjective plus a field-naming ending, and its root also builds the family of language words.
intro.cn: 这个词是形容词加表领域的词尾构成，其词根也构成「语言」一词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin lingua supplies the root; the Greek-derived ending for fields passed through Latin and French before English fixed the name.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 lingua 提供词根；表领域的希腊来源词尾经拉丁语与法语，最终在英语中定名。

items.example: The root names both the organ and its product.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根兼指器官与其产物。

items.structure: Greek-derived ending for fields of study
items.example: The ending builds names such as physics and ethics.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾构成「物理学」「伦理学」等名称。

items.example: The linguist analysed the vowel system.
items.exampleCN: 这位语言学家分析了元音系统。

items.meaning: of language or of the field
items.example: Linguistic data filled three notebooks.
items.exampleCN: 语言数据填满了三个笔记本。

items.example: Linguistics became independent of literary study.
items.exampleCN: 语言学从文学研究中独立出来。

items.example: Sociolinguistics maps speech to class and region.
items.exampleCN: 社会语言学把言语与阶层、地区对应起来。

items.example: Psycholinguistics studies how sentences are understood.
items.exampleCN: 心理语言学研究会话如何被理解。

items.example: Computational linguistics builds parsing tools.
items.exampleCN: 计算语言学构建句法分析工具。

definition_zh: 语言学家；（宽泛地）通晓多种语言的人
definition_en: a person who studies language scientifically, or more loosely a person who knows several languages
core_image: 一位研究者坐在野外折叠椅上，膝上放着录音笔与写满记号的笔记本，面前的老人正对着麦克风说话
scene: 野外的折叠椅上坐着一位研究者，膝上放着录音笔与写满记号的笔记本。The linguist spent three seasons recording a language with fewer than forty speakers.
sceneCN: 这里指「以科学方法研究语言的人」（第 1 个义项：语言研究者）；句意为这位研究者用了三个季节，记录一种使用者不足四十人的语言。可辨识物件：折叠椅、录音笔、笔记本、麦克风。

pos.zh: 语言学家；通晓多种语言的人（可数）

senses.title: A scientific student of language
senses.titleCN: 以科学方法研究语言的人
senses.definition: a person who studies the structure, history or use of language as a researcher
senses.definitionCN: 以研究者身份研究语言结构、历史或使用的人
senses.example: The linguist argued that no dialect is grammatically inferior.
senses.exampleCN: 这位语言学家主张，没有哪种方言在语法上更低劣。
senses.why: the word began as a name for someone skilled in languages and was narrowed to the scientific sense in the nineteenth century.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指精通语言的人，十九世纪才收窄为科学研究者的意思。

senses.title: A specialist in one language or family
senses.titleCN: 某一语言或语系的专家
senses.definition: a scholar whose expertise is a particular language, family or region
senses.definitionCN: 专长于某一语言、语系或地区的学者
senses.example: A specialist in the family identified the inscription within a day.
senses.exampleCN: 一位熟悉该语系的专家一天之内就辨认出这段铭文。
senses.why: specialization is the everyday form that the general title takes inside universities.
senses.whyCN: 在大学内部，这个通称最常见的形态就是「专精某一领域」。

senses.title: A person who knows many languages
senses.definition: a loose everyday use for someone fluent in several languages
senses.definitionCN: 日常宽泛用法，指能流利使用多种语言的人
senses.example: He was a fine linguist, at ease in six or seven languages.
senses.exampleCN: 他是位出色的语言通，六七种语言都说得自在。
senses.why: the older sense survives because knowing many tongues was once the clearest proof of skill with language.
senses.whyCN: 旧义仍然留存，因为通晓多语曾是语言能力最明显的证明。

senses.title: A historical linguist
senses.definition: a researcher who reconstructs how languages changed and split in the past
senses.definitionCN: 重构语言过去如何变化与分化的研究者
senses.example: The historical linguist traced the word back to an older root.
senses.exampleCN: 这位历史语言学家把这个词追到一个更古老的词根。
senses.why: reconstructing the past is a distinct craft inside the field, and its practitioners keep the general title.
senses.whyCN: 重构过去是学科内一门独立技艺，其从业者沿用通称。

senses.title: A descriptive field worker
senses.titleCN: 做田野描写的语言调查者
senses.definition: a researcher who records a language by working with its speakers
senses.definitionCN: 通过与使用者合作来记录一种语言的研究者
senses.example: Field linguists wrote down songs no outsider had heard.
senses.exampleCN: 田野语言学家记录下外来者从未听过的歌。
senses.why: the discipline needed people to go where the language was spoken, and the title went with them.
senses.whyCN: 这门学科需要有人到说这种语言的地方去，这个称号也随之而去。

senses.title: A computational linguist
senses.definition: a researcher who builds computational models of language
senses.definitionCN: 建立语言计算模型的研究者
senses.example: The computational linguist trained the parser on a new corpus.
senses.exampleCN: 这位计算语言学家在新的语料上训练句法分析器。
senses.why: the field's models had to be implementable, which created a new kind of practitioner.
senses.whyCN: 学科的模型必须可实现，于是产生了一类新的从业者。

senses.title: An applied linguist
senses.definition: a researcher who applies linguistic findings to teaching, medicine or policy
senses.definitionCN: 把语言学成果用于教学、医疗或政策的研究者
senses.example: An applied linguist redesigned the reading test.
senses.exampleCN: 一位应用语言学家重新设计了阅读测试。
senses.why: findings had to travel into classrooms and clinics, so applied work acquired the title.
senses.whyCN: 研究成果必须进入课堂与诊所，应用工作因此获得了这个称号。

senses.title: A forensic linguist
senses.definition: a specialist who analyses wording as evidence in legal cases
senses.definitionCN: 在法律案件中把措辞当作证据分析的专家
senses.example: The forensic linguist compared the ransom note with the suspect's letters.
senses.exampleCN: 司法语言学家把勒索信与嫌疑人的书信作了比对。
senses.why: courts needed a reader of wording, and the discipline supplied one.
senses.whyCN: 法庭需要有人读懂措辞，学科便提供了这样的人。

intro.en: Linguist comes from Latin lingua 'tongue, language' plus the person-ending -ista, probably through French. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁 lingua「舌头、语言」加表人的词尾，很可能经法语传入。年代均为约数。

items.en: Lingua meant 'tongue' and 'language'. Its deeper origin is unsettled and no older form is attested.
items.cn: lingua 兼指「舌头」与「语言」，更深来源无定论，也没有更早形式的书证。

items.en: The ending -ista named a person concerned with something, and passed into French and English as a marker of occupation or skill.
items.cn: 表人的词尾指从事某事的人，经法语与英语成为职业或技能的标记。

items.en: In the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries a linguist was simply someone skilled in languages, often a traveller or a clergyman.
items.cn: 在十七与十八世纪，这个词只指精通语言的人，常是旅行者或神职人员。

items.en: Nineteenth-century comparative philology gave the word its modern academic meaning, the student of language as a science.
items.cn: 十九世纪的比较语文学赋予它现代学术含义，即把语言作为科学来研究的人。

items.en: The twentieth century produced historical, field, computational, applied and forensic linguists as the field divided its labour.
items.cn: 二十世纪随着学科分工，出现了历史、田野、计算、应用与司法语言学家等称号。

items.en: Source uncertain: the pre-Latin root is unknown, and the first English use of the scientific sense is dated only approximately.
items.cn: 来源不确定：拉丁语之前的词根不明，这个科学义在英语中最早使用的年代只能约略推定。

note.en: Group one holds the same-root forms that are easily mistaken for the person; group two holds people described by their command of languages.
note.cn: 第一组是同根、容易被误当作「人」的词形；第二组是以语言能力来描述的人。

entries.definition: The discipline, not a person in it; a linguist works inside linguistics.
entries.definitionCN: 指学科，而非学科中的人；语言学家在语言学内部工作。

entries.definition: Describes what relates to language; it cannot name a person.
entries.definitionCN: 描述与语言有关的性质，不能指人。

entries.definition: The system under study; a linguist studies language but is not one.
entries.definitionCN: 指被研究的系统；语言学家研究语言，但本身不是语言。

entries.definition: A scholar of texts and languages in the older tradition, close but not identical to a linguist.
entries.definitionCN: 旧传统中研究文本与语言的学者，与语言学家接近但不相同。

entries.definition: A person who speaks many languages; the emphasis is on use, not research.
entries.definitionCN: 指会说多种语言的人，重点在使用，而非研究。

entries.definition: A person who turns writing from one language into another; skill in languages is a tool, not a science.
entries.definitionCN: 指把文字从一种语言转换为另一种的人；语言能力是工具，不是科学。

entries.definition: A person who renders speech live between languages, a practical rather than academic role.
entries.definitionCN: 指现场口译的人，属实务而非学术角色。

entries.definition: A specialist in word origins, a narrow branch of linguistic work.
entries.definitionCN: 指专研词源的学者，是语言工作中较窄的一支。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real related words, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实相关词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The root means tongue, and the ending marks a person, so the word is literally a tongue-person.
normal.cn: 词根意为「舌头」，词尾标记人，因此这个词字面上就是「摆弄舌头的人」。

normal.en: Fixed phrases add the specialty: field, historical, computational, forensic.
normal.cn: 固定搭配补上专长：田野、历史、计算、司法。

normal.en: The everyday sense of a multilingual person is older than the academic sense.
normal.cn: 「会说多语的人」这一日常义，比学术义更古老。

normal.en: The family runs language, linguistic, linguistics, bilingual, multilingual.
normal.cn: 同族包括「语言」「语言的」「语言学」「双语的」「多语的」。

normal.en: The plural simply adds one ending, so counts of researchers are easy to form.
normal.cn: 复数只加一个词尾，统计研究者人数很容易。

abstract.en: Picture a person with a notebook in a village where only a few old speakers remain.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人带着笔记本，走进只剩几位年长说话者的村子。

abstract.en: Picture a tongue turned into a measuring instrument.
abstract.cn: 想象舌头被改造成一件测量工具。

abstract.en: Picture a detective who reads wording instead of footprints.
abstract.cn: 想象一位读措辞而不读脚印的侦探。

examples.en: The linguist published a grammar of a language with no written tradition.
examples.cn: 这位语言学家出版了一种没有书写传统语言的语法。

examples.en: A good linguist listens before proposing a rule.
examples.cn: 好的语言学家先倾听，再提出规则。

examples.en: The court hired a linguist to compare the two letters.
examples.cn: 法庭聘请了一位语言学家来比对这两封信。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「林归斯特」——把林子里的方言归拢起来研究的那个人，就是语言学家。

root: 拉丁 lingua「舌头、语言」加表人的词尾，经法语进入英语；早期指精通语言的人，十九世纪比较语文学兴起后收窄为以科学方法研究语言的人。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses describe one person from several directions: the researcher, the specialist, the multilingual, then the historical, field, computational, applied and forensic versions of the role.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从多个方向描述同一个人：研究者、专精者、通晓多语者，然后是历史、田野、计算、应用与司法等不同版本的角色。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a folding chair in the field, a recorder, and a notebook full of marks.
core.cn: 核心意象：野外的折叠椅、录音笔，以及写满记号的笔记本。

branches.en: THE CORE ROLE: a scientific student of language is the modern centre of the word.
branches.cn: 核心角色：以科学方法研究语言的人，是这个词的现代中心。

branches.en: NARROW EXPERTISE: universities turn the general title into specialists in one family.
branches.cn: 狭窄专长：大学把这个通称变成某一语系的专家。

branches.en: THE OLDER SENSE: knowing many languages still counts as being a linguist in ordinary speech.
branches.cn: 较旧的含义：在日常说法里，通晓多语仍算语言学家。

branches.en: PAST AND PRESENT SPEAKERS: some reconstruct history, others record living speech.
branches.cn: 过去的与现在的说话者：有人重构历史，有人记录活的语言。

branches.en: WORKING ROLES: machines, classrooms and courtrooms each employ the title.
branches.cn: 工作中的角色：机器、课堂与法庭各自雇用这个称号。

intro.en: The word is a Latin root plus a person-ending, and the same root builds the whole family of language terms.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁词根加表人的词尾构成，同一词根也构成整套「语言」术语。

latinIntro.en: Latin lingua gives the root, and the person-ending entered English through French; the same pair builds names for practitioners in many fields.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 lingua 提供词根，表人的词尾经法语进入英语；同一组合也为许多领域的从业者造名。

items.example: The root names the object the person works on.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根指此人所研究的对象。

items.example: The ending turns a field into a person who works in it.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把领域变成在其中工作的人。

items.example: Language is what the linguist studies.
items.exampleCN: 语言是语言学家研究的东西。

items.example: Linguistic evidence supported the claim.
items.exampleCN: 语言证据支持了这一主张。

items.example: Linguistics trains new linguists.
items.exampleCN: 语言学培养新的语言学家。

items.example: A bilingual informant checked the translation.
items.exampleCN: 一位双语发音人核对了译文。

items.example: Multilingual editors joined the project.
items.exampleCN: 多语编辑加入了项目。

items.example: The trade lingo puzzled the new apprentice.
items.exampleCN: 行业行话让新学徒摸不着头脑。

definition_zh: 方言；地方话；（某一群体或行业的）特定说法
definition_en: a regional or social variety of a language, or a specialized way of speaking within a group
core_image: 两个相邻村子的集市，一边摊主把同一个词说成两种腔调，中间只隔着一条浅溪
scene: 浅溪两侧各有一个集市，两边摊主把同一个词说出两种腔调。The dialect on the far bank was still understandable, though every vowel had shifted.
sceneCN: 这里指「一种语言的地方变体」（第 1 个义项：按地区分化出的说法）；句意为对岸的方言仍听得懂，只是每个元音都变了。可辨识物件：集市、浅溪、摊主、两种腔调。

senses.title: A regional variety of a language
senses.titleCN: 一种语言按地区分化出的变体
senses.definition: a form of a language spoken in one area, differing in pronunciation, words or grammar
senses.definitionCN: 在某一地区使用的语言形式，在发音、词汇或语法上有所不同
senses.example: The dialect of the northern valley keeps words lost elsewhere.
senses.exampleCN: 北部山谷的方言保留了别处已经消失的词。
senses.why: the Greek source meant the speech of a particular place or group, so region is the oldest layer.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语来源指某一地点或群体的说话方式，因此「地区」是最古老的一层。

senses.title: A social dialect tied to a group
senses.titleCN: 与某一群体绑定的社会方言
senses.definition: a variety associated with a class, occupation or age group rather than a place
senses.definitionCN: 与阶层、职业或年龄群体相关，而非与地点相关的变体
senses.example: The social dialect of the dockyards had its own words for tides.
senses.exampleCN: 船坞一带的社会方言有自己的潮汐用语。
senses.why: once region was seen to be only one cause of variation, group membership took the same label.
senses.whyCN: 当人们发现地区只是变异的一种原因，群体归属也用了同一个标签。

senses.title: A nonstandard way of speaking
senses.titleCN: 被视为不标准的说话方式
senses.definition: a variety treated as less correct than the standard, often with a critical tone
senses.definitionCN: 被认为不如标准形式正确的变体，常带批评语气
senses.example: Calling the village speech a dialect was itself a judgement.
senses.exampleCN: 把这村子的说话方式称作方言，本身就是一种评判。
senses.why: standardization created a centre, and everything away from it was labelled with the older word.
senses.whyCN: 标准化造出一个中心，凡离开中心者都被贴上这个旧词。

senses.title: A variety on the border with a language
senses.definition: a variety whose status as dialect or language depends on politics rather than structure
senses.definitionCN: 其「方言或语言」地位取决于政治而非结构的变体
senses.example: Whether Low German is a dialect or a language is a political question.
senses.exampleCN: 低地德语是方言还是语言，是一个政治问题。
senses.why: structure cannot decide the matter, so the word keeps a border that only politics can draw.
senses.whyCN: 结构无法决定这件事，因此这个词保留了一条只有政治能划出的边界。

senses.title: A point on a continuum
senses.definition: one point in a chain of varieties that shade into each other across distance
senses.definitionCN: 在一串随距离彼此渐变的变体中的一个点
senses.example: Along the coast each harbour spoke a slightly different dialect.
senses.exampleCN: 沿海每个港口都说着略不相同的方言。
senses.why: linguists replaced sharp borders with continua, and the word came to name a position on the line.
senses.whyCN: 语言学家用连续体取代清晰边界，这个词于是指线上的一个位置。

senses.title: An older regional form preserved in texts
senses.titleCN: 文献中保存的较早地方形式
senses.definition: the regional speech of an earlier period, studied in old writings
senses.definitionCN: 较早时期的地方说法，通过旧文献研究
senses.example: The play preserves a dialect of the sixteenth century.
senses.exampleCN: 这部戏剧保存了十六世纪的一种方言。
senses.why: writing can freeze speech that has since changed, so the word also names what old texts preserve.
senses.whyCN: 文字能冻住后来已变的言语，因此这个词也指旧文本保存下来的东西。

senses.title: Dialect used as literary material
senses.titleCN: 被用作文学材料的方言
senses.definition: a regional variety deliberately used in poetry or fiction for texture and place
senses.definitionCN: 在诗歌或小说中刻意使用、以增质地与地方感的地方说法
senses.example: Her poems move between standard speech and the dialect of her grandmother.
senses.exampleCN: 她的诗在标准语与祖母的方言之间来回移动。
senses.why: a variety valued for its local weight can be used deliberately, and the same word serves that purpose.
senses.whyCN: 一种因地方分量而受重视的变体可被刻意使用，同一个词也服务于这个目的。

senses.title: A variant inside a larger system
senses.titleCN: 较大体系内部的一种变体
senses.definition: one recognized variant of a formal system, such as a dialect of a programming language
senses.definitionCN: 某一形式体系中获承认的变体，如某种编程语言的方言
senses.example: The old software speaks a dialect of the language that no manual describes.
senses.exampleCN: 这套旧软件说的是该语言的一种无手册记载的方言。
senses.why: the word's shape, a variety within a larger tongue, was borrowed for any rule-governed system.
senses.whyCN: 这个词「大体系内的变体」这一形态，被借用到任何受规则支配的系统。

intro.en: Dialect comes from Greek dialektos 'conversation, local speech', from dialegesthai 'to converse'. It reached English through Latin. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个词来自希腊 dialektos「交谈、地方话」，其动词为 dialegesthai「交谈」，经拉丁语进入英语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Dialegesthai meant 'to converse, discuss', built from a prefix meaning 'across, between' and a verb meaning 'to speak, to pick out words'.
items.cn: dialegesthai 意为「交谈、讨论」，由表「穿越、之间」的前缀与表「说话、拣选词语」的动词构成。

items.en: Dialektos named conversation itself and, by extension, the speech of a particular region or group.
items.cn: dialektos 指交谈本身，并引申指某一地区或群体的说话方式。

items.en: Latin borrowed the Greek word as dialectus, keeping the sense of a local form of speech.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入这个词，保留了「地方性说法」的含义。

items.en: English took the word in the sixteenth century, when scholars were comparing regional forms of Greek and English.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入，当时学者正在比较希腊语与英语的地方形式。

items.en: Twentieth-century sociolinguistics extended the word from places to social groups, producing the social dialect.
items.cn: 二十世纪的社会语言学把这个词从地点扩展到社会群体，产生「社会方言」。

items.en: Source uncertain: the deeper pre-Greek origin of the speaking verb is not established, and the exact first English use is dated only approximately.
items.cn: 来源不确定：那个表「说话」的动词在希腊语之前的更深来源未获证明，其英语首见年代也只能约略推定。

note.en: Group one holds words that look or sound close and are often confused; group two holds near neighbours in the study of variation.
note.cn: 第一组是外形或读音接近、常被混淆的词；第二组是变异研究中的近邻概念。

entries.definition: Relating to logical debate or to tension between ideas; it shares the Greek root but not the meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 指逻辑论辩或观念张力，共享希腊词根，但意思不同。

entries.definition: A conversation between two or more people; it is the root's plain sense, not a regional variety.
entries.definitionCN: 指两人或多人之间的交谈，是词根的本义，并非地区变体。

entries.definition: The sound pattern of a speaker; a dialect also includes words and grammar.
entries.definitionCN: 指说话者的发音模式；方言还包括词汇与语法。

entries.definition: The speech habits of a single individual, the smallest unit of variation.
entries.definitionCN: 指单个人的言语习惯，是变异的最小单位。

entries.definition: The whole system that a dialect belongs to; the line between the two is often political.
entries.definitionCN: 指方言所属的整个系统；两者之间的界线常是政治性的。

entries.definition: A neutral technical word for any form of a language, avoiding the stigma that dialect can carry.
entries.definitionCN: 指语言任何形式的中性术语，避开「方言」可能带来的贬义。

entries.definition: A word or form peculiar to a region, a single item rather than a whole variety.
entries.definitionCN: 指某地区特有的词或形式，是单项而非整套变体。

entries.definition: An informal or rural local speech, often used with a slightly dismissive tone.
entries.definitionCN: 指非正式或乡村的本地话，常带轻微轻视语气。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real related words, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实相关词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The Greek root means conversation, so a dialect is first the way a place talks.
normal.cn: 希腊词根意为「交谈」，因此方言首先是某地说话的方式。

normal.en: Fixed phrases attach it to place and group: regional dialect, social dialect.
normal.cn: 固定搭配把它挂到地点与群体：地区方言、社会方言。

normal.en: The look-alike word for logical debate differs by one syllable and a different ending.
normal.cn: 那个表逻辑论辩的形近词只差一个音节与一个不同词尾。

normal.en: The family runs dialectal, dialectology, dialectologist, dialogue.
normal.cn: 同族包括「方言的」「方言学」「方言学家」「对话」。

normal.en: A dialect can be a whole variety or a single local word, depending on the writer.
normal.cn: 方言既可指整套变体，也可指单个地方词，视作者而定。

abstract.en: Picture one stream between two markets, each bank pronouncing the same word differently.
abstract.cn: 想象两个集市之间隔着一条浅溪，两岸把同一个词说得不一样。

abstract.en: Picture a road where each milepost changes the vowel slightly.
abstract.cn: 想象一条路，每个里程碑都让元音略变一点。

abstract.en: Picture a family recipe that each kitchen makes with its own measure.
abstract.cn: 想象一份家常食谱，每家厨房都用自己的分量做。

examples.en: The two villages are a mile apart but speak different dialects.
examples.cn: 两个村子相隔一英里，却说着不同的方言。

examples.en: Radio broadcasting pushed the standard dialect into every home.
examples.cn: 广播把标准方言推进了每一户人家。

examples.en: A dialect is a full system, not a broken version of the standard.
examples.cn: 方言是一套完整的系统，而不是标准语的破损版本。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「带而来克特」——带着本地腔调而来的那种说法，就是方言。

root: 希腊 dialektos「交谈、地方话」出自 dialegesthai「交谈」，由表「之间」的前缀与表「说话」的动词构成；经拉丁语进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from a place to a group, then to stigma, political borders, continua, old texts, literature and finally to any variant inside a larger system.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从地点走向群体，再到污名、政治边界、连续体、旧文献、文学，最后指向任何较大体系内部的变体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one stream, two markets, the same word in two accents.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条浅溪、两个集市，同一个词两种腔调。

branches.en: PLACE FIRST: the oldest layer is the speech of one region.
branches.cn: 地点优先：最古老的一层是一个地区的说话方式。

branches.en: GROUP NEXT: class and occupation produce varieties that sound like places.
branches.cn: 群体其次：阶层与职业产生听起来像「地方」的变体。

branches.en: THE LABEL AS JUDGEMENT: calling speech a dialect can itself rank it lower.
branches.cn: 标签即评判：把某话称作方言，本身就可能把它排低。

branches.en: BORDERS AND BRIDGES: status is political, while varieties actually shade into one another.
branches.cn: 边界与桥梁：地位是政治问题，而变体实际彼此渐变。

branches.en: OLD TEXTS, NEW USES: earlier speech survives in writing, writers use it, and other systems have their own.
branches.cn: 旧文本与新用途：早期说法在文字中存活，作家使用它，其他体系也有自己的变体。

intro.en: The word is a Greek compound carried into English through Latin, so its two parts can be read separately.
intro.cn: 这个词是经拉丁语进入英语的希腊复合词，两部分可以分开读。

latinIntro.en: Greek dia- 'across, between' and legein 'to speak, gather words' built the noun; Latin dialectus passed it to English.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语表「之间」的前缀与表「说话、汇集词语」的动词构成该名词，拉丁语再把它传给英语。

items.example: The prefix sets the word between speakers.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把词放在说话者「之间」。

items.structure: Greek verb, 'to speak, gather, pick out'
items.example: The root carries both talking and choosing.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根兼带「说话」与「拣选」。

items.example: The verb names talk that passes between people.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词指在人与人之间进行的谈话。

items.example: The noun shifted from talk to the talk of a place.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词从「交谈」转到「某地的话」。

items.example: The northern dialect keeps older vowels.
items.exampleCN: 北部方言保留较旧的元音。

items.example: Dialectal forms appear in the margin.
items.exampleCN: 方言形式出现在页边。

items.example: Dialectology mapped the county's vowels.
items.exampleCN: 方言学绘制了这个县的元音分布。

items.example: The two leaders opened a dialogue.
items.exampleCN: 两位领导人开启了对话。

definition_zh: 多语的；使用多种语言的；多种语言并存的
definition_en: using or involving several languages, or able to speak several languages
core_image: 一块立在中转站的分区指示牌，同一行信息用四五种文字并排写出，行人抬头寻找自己的那一行
scene: 中转站的走廊上立着一块分区指示牌，同一行信息用四五种文字并排写出。A multilingual notice board greeted arrivals in every language spoken along the route.
sceneCN: 这里指「同时使用多种语言的」（第 1 个义项：涉及多种语言并用）；句意为一块多语告示牌用沿线路途所讲的每种语言迎接抵达者。可辨识物件：指示牌、多行文字、走廊、行人。

pos.zh: 多语的；使用多种语言的
使用多种语言的人（较少用）

senses.title: Using several languages
senses.definition: describing a person, group or thing that works in more than two languages
senses.definitionCN: 描述在两种以上语言中运作的人、群体或事物
senses.example: The reception desk is multilingual and answers in four tongues.
senses.exampleCN: 前台是多语的，能用四种语言应答。
senses.why: the word joins a prefix for 'many' to the root for language, so it simply counts tongues.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把表「许多」的前缀与表「语言」的词根相连，因此它只是数语言的数目。

senses.title: A society with many languages
senses.definition: describing a community in which several languages are in daily use
senses.definitionCN: 描述若干语言在日常中同时使用的社群
senses.example: A multilingual city can hold five languages in one market.
senses.exampleCN: 一座多语城市可以在一个市场里容纳五种语言。
senses.why: a city that keeps several tongues in daily use is the plural of a bilingual town, so the same adjective covers it.
senses.whyCN: 一座日常使用几种语言的城市，是双语城镇的复数形态，同一形容词自然覆盖。

senses.title: A text or sign in several languages
senses.titleCN: 用多种语言写成的文本或标牌
senses.definition: written or printed in more than two languages at once
senses.definitionCN: 同时以两种以上语言书写或印刷
senses.example: The airport's multilingual signs were redesigned after the survey.
senses.exampleCN: 调查之后，机场的多语标牌重新设计过。
senses.why: the count becomes visible when the same words are printed side by side.
senses.whyCN: 当同一段话并排印出时，那个数目就变得可见。

senses.title: Multilingual education
senses.definition: schooling that uses several languages as media of instruction
senses.definitionCN: 以多种语言作为教学语言的教育
senses.example: Multilingual education let children begin in the language of home.
senses.exampleCN: 多语教育让孩子从家里的语言开始学。
senses.why: a school that teaches through several tongues makes the count a policy.
senses.whyCN: 用几种语言教学的学校，把这个数目变成了政策。

senses.title: Multilingual software
senses.definition: describing a program or platform that handles several languages
senses.definitionCN: 描述能处理多种语言的程序或平台
senses.example: The multilingual platform switched language with one click.
senses.exampleCN: 这个多语平台一键就能切换语言。
senses.why: software can hold several language packs, so the old adjective was extended to code.
senses.whyCN: 软件可以装几套语言包，这个旧形容词因此被扩展到代码。

senses.title: Multilingual processing in the mind
senses.definition: describing research on how a mind stores and switches among several languages
senses.definitionCN: 描述对心智如何储存并切换多种语言的研究
senses.example: Multilingual speakers activate both lexicons at once.
senses.exampleCN: 多语说话者会同时激活两套词库。
senses.why: researchers ask whether the languages compete or cooperate, and the adjective names the case.
senses.whyCN: 研究者追问这些语言是竞争还是协作，这个形容词就指这种情形。

senses.title: A multilingual workplace
senses.definition: describing an organization whose staff routinely work across languages
senses.definitionCN: 描述员工日常跨语言工作的组织
senses.example: The hospital runs a multilingual helpline for new arrivals.
senses.exampleCN: 这家医院为新到者开设多语求助热线。
senses.why: staff who answer in several tongues turn the adjective into a job requirement.
senses.whyCN: 用几种语言应答的员工，把这个形容词变成一项岗位要求。

senses.title: Multilingual resources
senses.definition: describing dictionaries, corpora or services provided in several languages
senses.definitionCN: 描述以多种语言提供的词典、语料或服务
senses.example: The archive released multilingual finding aids.
senses.exampleCN: 档案馆发布了多语检索工具。
senses.why: once records and tools multiply languages, the word describes the shelf rather than the speaker.
senses.whyCN: 当记录与工具成倍增加语言，这个词便描述书架而非说话者。

intro.en: Multilingual joins multi- 'many', from Latin multus, to Latin lingua 'tongue, language' and the adjective ending -al. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个词把表「许多」的前缀与拉丁 lingua「舌头、语言」及形容词词尾相连；该前缀出自拉丁 multus。年代均为约数。

items.en: Multus meant 'much, many'. Its comparative and related forms also gave English multi- as a combining element.
items.cn: multus 意为「多的、许多的」，其比较级与相关形式也为英语提供了表「多」的组合成分。

items.en: Lingua meant 'tongue' and 'language'; its deeper origin is unsettled and no older attested form is agreed.
items.cn: lingua 兼指「舌头」与「语言」；其更深来源无定论，也没有公认的更早书证形式。

items.en: The ending -alis built relational adjectives in Latin, and English -al does the same work.
items.cn: 拉丁语用形容词词尾构成关系形容词，英语的对应词尾承担同样的功能。

items.en: English formed the adjective in the nineteenth century, when travel, trade and empire made many-language contact ordinary.
items.cn: 英语在十九世纪构成这个形容词，当时旅行、贸易与帝国使多语接触成为常态。

items.en: The late twentieth century applied it to software, education policy and brain research.
items.cn: 二十世纪后期，它被用于软件、教育政策与脑研究。

items.en: Source uncertain: the first printed use of the English adjective is not precisely dated, and the pre-Latin root remains unknown.
items.cn: 来源不确定：这个英语形容词最早的印刷使用年代不明，其在拉丁语之前的词根亦未知。

note.en: Group one holds the numbering words for how many languages are used; group two holds terms about language arrangements.
note.cn: 第一组是按语言数量编号的词；第二组是关于语言安排的术语。

entries.definition: Using exactly two languages; multilingual means more than two and often leaves the count open.
entries.definitionCN: 指正好使用两种语言；多语则指多于两种，且常不限定具体数目。

entries.definition: Using a single language; it is the opposite pole and often appears in research contrasts.
entries.definitionCN: 指只使用一种语言，是相反的一极，常用于研究对照。

entries.definition: The state or practice of using many languages; the adjective describes what the noun names.
entries.definitionCN: 指多语并存的状态或实践；形容词则描述名词所指的情形。

entries.definition: A person who speaks many languages, or an adjective for such a person; it stresses personal skill.
entries.definitionCN: 指会说多种语言的人，或描述此人的形容词，强调个人能力。

entries.definition: Relating to several cultures; a society can be multicultural while sharing one language.
entries.definitionCN: 指涉及多种文化；一个社会可以共享一种语言而同时是多文化的。

entries.definition: A term favoured in European policy for a person's partial skills across several languages.
entries.definitionCN: 欧洲政策偏好的说法，指个人在多种语言上各自不完整的技能。

entries.definition: The rules a state adopts about which languages it will use; the adjective alone does not imply policy.
entries.definitionCN: 指国家对使用哪些语言所作的规定；单用形容词并不含政策义。

entries.definition: The act of turning text from one language into another; multilingual describes the result, not the act.
entries.definitionCN: 指把文本从一种语言转为另一种；多语描述结果，而非动作。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real related words, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实相关词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The first element means many, the second means tongue, so the word counts languages.
normal.cn: 第一个成分意为「多」，第二个意为「舌头」，因此这个词是在数语言。

normal.en: Fixed phrases attach it to institutions: multilingual society, education, staff.
normal.cn: 固定搭配把它挂到机构上：多语社会、多语教育、多语员工。

normal.en: It stands above bilingual in a simple ladder: one, two, many.
normal.cn: 它在简单的阶梯上高于「双语的」：单语、双语、多语。

normal.en: The family runs multilingualism, multilingually, bilingual, monolingual.
normal.cn: 同族包括「多语现象」「以多语方式」「双语的」「单语的」。

normal.en: A station sign with several scripts is the clearest picture of the word.
normal.cn: 写着几种文字的车站标牌，是这个词最清楚的画面。

abstract.en: Picture a single corridor where every passenger hears a different welcome.
abstract.cn: 想象一条走廊，每位乘客都听到不同的欢迎语。

abstract.en: Picture five doors into one room, each opened by a different key.
abstract.cn: 想象通向同一房间的五道门，每道由不同的钥匙打开。

abstract.en: Picture a brain holding several maps of the same city.
abstract.cn: 想象一个头脑里装着同一座城市的几张地图。

examples.en: The region has been multilingual for centuries, not only since tourism.
examples.cn: 这个地区几百年来一直多语并存，并非只因旅游业才如此。

examples.en: Multilingual ballots are required wherever literacy is uneven.
examples.cn: 在识字程度不均的地方，须提供多语选票。

examples.en: A multilingual corpus makes it possible to compare idioms across languages.
examples.cn: 多语语料库使跨语言比较习语成为可能。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「马提林圭尔」——马背上驮着许多种语言一路走，这就是多语的。

root: 表「许多」的前缀出自拉丁 multus「多的」，后接拉丁 lingua「舌头、语言」与形容词词尾；十九世纪英语构成该形容词，指使用或涉及多种语言。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses take one count and spread it across persons, cities, signs, schools, software, minds, workplaces and archives.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项拿同一个数目向外铺开：人、城市、标牌、学校、软件、心智、工作场所与档案馆。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one sign board whose every line appears in four or five scripts.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块指示牌，每一行都用四五种文字并排写出。

branches.en: THE COUNT AND THE MIND: more than two languages, held and used by one person.
branches.cn: 数目与心智：多于两种语言，由一个人持有并使用。

branches.en: A PLACE: cities and regions can hold several languages at once.
branches.cn: 一个地方：城市与地区可以同时容纳几种语言。

branches.en: A SURFACE: signs and documents show the count where everyone can see it.
branches.cn: 一个表面：标牌与文书把这个数目摆到人人可见之处。

branches.en: INSTITUTIONS: schools teach in several tongues, and workplaces answer in several.
branches.cn: 机构：学校用几种语言教学，工作场所用几种语言应答。

branches.en: TOOLS AND RECORDS: software and archives multiply the languages they carry.
branches.cn: 工具与记录：软件与档案馆成倍扩大其承载的语言。

intro.en: The word is a prefix plus a Latin root plus an adjective ending, and each part also builds a family.
intro.cn: 这个词由前缀、拉丁词根与形容词词尾构成，每一部分也都构成一族词。

latinIntro.en: Latin multus supplies the counting prefix, Latin lingua the language root; English -al mirrors the Latin adjective ending.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 multus 提供表数量的前缀，拉丁 lingua 提供「语言」词根；英语词尾对应拉丁形容词词尾。

items.example: The prefix answers the question how many.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀回答「有多少」。

items.example: The root names what is counted.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根指被计数的东西。

items.example: The ending turns the count into a description.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把数目变成描述。

items.example: The office keeps multilingual records.
items.exampleCN: 这个办公室保存多语记录。

items.example: Multilingualism is normal in border towns.
items.exampleCN: 在边境城镇，多语并存是常态。

items.example: The guide was written multilingually.
items.exampleCN: 这本指南以多语写成。

items.example: Bilingual staff covered the night desk.
items.exampleCN: 双语员工值守夜班台。

items.example: Monolingual forms excluded half the residents.
items.exampleCN: 单语表格把一半居民排除在外。

definition_zh: 双语的；使用两种语言的；双语并用的（也可作名词：双语者）
definition_en: using or written in two languages, or able to speak two languages
core_image: 一张对开的告示纸，左半边与右半边写着同样内容却用两种文字，中间用一条细线分开
scene: 社区公告栏上贴着一张对开的告示，左右两半内容相同，文字却不同。Every bilingual form in the office carried the same sentence twice.
sceneCN: 这里指「同时使用两种语言的」（第 1 个义项：涉及两种语言并用）；句意为办公室里的每份双语表格都把同一句话写了两遍。可辨识物件：告示、对开纸、两种文字、公告栏。

pos.zh: 双语的；使用两种语言的

senses.title: Using two languages
senses.definition: describing a thing, service or activity that works in two languages
senses.definitionCN: 描述以两种语言运作的事物、服务或活动
senses.example: The bilingual help desk answers in Mandarin and English.
senses.exampleCN: 双语服务台用普通话与英语应答。
senses.why: the word pairs a prefix for 'two' with the Latin word for tongue, so it counts two languages exactly.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把表「二」的前缀与拉丁语表「舌头」的词相连，精确地数两种语言。

senses.title: A person who speaks two languages
senses.definition: describing someone who can use two languages in daily life
senses.definitionCN: 描述能在日常生活中使用两种语言的人
senses.example: She grew up bilingual and still dreams in both.
senses.exampleCN: 她从小双语成长，至今仍用两种语言做梦。
senses.why: a person who carries the pair through a whole life is the human face of the count.
senses.whyCN: 把这一对语言带过一生的人，是这个数目的「人面」。

senses.title: A text or sign in two languages
senses.titleCN: 用两种语言写成的文本或标牌
senses.definition: printed or displayed in two languages at once
senses.definitionCN: 同时以两种语言印刷或展示
senses.example: The bilingual label lists every ingredient twice.
senses.exampleCN: 双语标签把每种成分列出两遍。
senses.why: two languages printed side by side make the pair visible.
senses.whyCN: 两种语言并排印出，就让这一对变得可见。

senses.title: Bilingual education
senses.definition: schooling in which two languages serve as media of instruction
senses.definitionCN: 以两种语言作为教学语言的教育
senses.example: Bilingual education delayed the shift to the majority language.
senses.exampleCN: 双语教育推迟了向多数语言的转换。
senses.why: a school that teaches in two languages turns the count into a curriculum.
senses.whyCN: 用两种语言教学的学校，把这个数目变成课程。

senses.title: A bilingual community or region
senses.definition: describing a place where two languages are in everyday use
senses.definitionCN: 描述两种语言在日常中并用的地方
senses.example: The valley has been bilingual since the railway arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 铁路开通以来，这条山谷一直双语并存。
senses.why: a whole place can hold the pair for generations, so the adjective describes geography as well as people.
senses.whyCN: 整个地方能把这一对保留几代，因此这个形容词既描述人也描述地理。

senses.title: Bilingual processing in the mind
senses.definition: describing research on how one mind stores and switches between two languages
senses.definitionCN: 描述对同一心智如何储存并切换两种语言的研究
senses.example: Bilingual speakers separate their languages by context, not by effort.
senses.exampleCN: 双语说话者按场合区分语言，而不是靠费力控制。
senses.why: a mind that holds two systems is the pair studied from inside.
senses.whyCN: 容纳两套系统的心智，是从内部研究的「这一对」。

senses.title: A bilingual dictionary or resource
senses.definition: a reference that gives equivalents in two languages
senses.definitionCN: 给出两种语言对应说法的工具书
senses.example: The bilingual dictionary marks which word fits which register.
senses.exampleCN: 这本双语词典标出哪个词属哪种语域。
senses.why: a dictionary exists to place one language beside the other.
senses.whyCN: 词典的存在，就是把一种语言放在另一种旁边。

senses.title: Bilingual policy or rights
senses.definition: describing official arrangements that guarantee services in two languages
senses.definitionCN: 描述保障以两种语言提供服务的官方安排
senses.example: Bilingual policy made every statute readable in both tongues.
senses.exampleCN: 双语政策使每项法规都能以两种语言阅读。
senses.why: a promise made in law must appear in both tongues, which turns the count into an obligation.
senses.whyCN: 法律作出的承诺必须以两种语言出现，这就把数目变成义务。

intro.en: Bilingual comes from Latin bilinguis 'two-tongued', built on bis 'twice' and lingua 'tongue, language'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁 bilinguis「双舌的」，由表「两次」的成分与 lingua「舌头、语言」构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Lingua meant 'tongue' and, by extension, 'language'. Its deeper origin is unsettled and no older attested form is agreed.
items.cn: lingua 指「舌头」，引申为「语言」。其更深来源无定论，也没有公认的更早书证形式。

items.en: Bilinguis meant 'two-tongued'. In Roman usage it could also mean 'double-tongued', that is, deceitful, a sense that English did not keep.
items.cn: bilinguis 意为「双舌的」。在罗马用法中它也可指「两面三刀的」，即欺骗性的，这一含义英语没有保留。

items.en: English formed the modern adjective in the nineteenth century, when schooling and censuses made two-language populations visible.
items.cn: 英语在十九世纪形成这个现代形容词，当时学校教育与人口普查使双语人群变得可见。

items.en: The twentieth century gave the word a policy life, naming programs that teach in two languages.
items.cn: 二十世纪赋予这个词政策生命，用来指以两种语言教学的项目。

items.en: Psychology and neuroscience later used it for the mental organisation of two language systems.
items.cn: 心理学与神经科学后来用它指两套语言系统在心智中的组织方式。

items.en: Source uncertain: the pre-Latin root is unknown, and the first English use of the modern sense is dated only approximately.
items.cn: 来源不确定：拉丁语之前的词根不明，这个现代义在英语中最早使用的年代只能约略推定。

note.en: Group one holds the counting words that are constantly confused; group two holds terms about two-language arrangements.
note.cn: 第一组是常被混淆的计数词；第二组是关于两种语言安排的术语。

entries.definition: Using several languages, often without a fixed count; bilingual is the exact two.
entries.definitionCN: 指使用多种语言，常不限定数目；双语则精确指两种。

entries.definition: Using a single language; it is the opposite pole of the same counting series.
entries.definitionCN: 指只使用一种语言，是同一计数序列的另一端。

entries.definition: The state or practice of having two languages; the adjective describes what the noun names.
entries.definitionCN: 指拥有两种语言的状态或实践；形容词则描述名词所指的情形。

entries.definition: A rare word for a person who speaks two languages; bilingual is far commoner as the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 指会说两种语言者的罕用名词；双语一词作名词更常见。

entries.definition: A common label for two-language school programs; it is a compound rather than a Latin borrowing.
entries.definitionCN: 指双语学校项目的常见标签，属复合词而非拉丁借词。

entries.definition: A literal English rendering of the Latin word; in older use it could also mean deceitful.
entries.definitionCN: 是那个拉丁词的直译英语说法；旧用法中也可指欺骗性的。

entries.definition: Using two dialects of one language, a narrower case than two separate languages.
entries.definitionCN: 指使用同一种语言的两种方言，范围比两种独立语言更窄。

entries.definition: The act of moving between languages in conversation; bilingual describes the capacity behind it.
entries.definitionCN: 指会话中在语言间切换的行为；双语描述其背后的能力。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real related words, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实相关词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The prefix means two and the root means tongue, so the word literally has two tongues.
normal.cn: 前缀意为「二」，词根意为「舌头」，因此这个词字面上就是「有两条舌头」。

normal.en: Fixed phrases attach it to services: bilingual signs, forms, help desk.
normal.cn: 固定搭配把它挂到服务上：双语标识、双语表格、双语服务台。

normal.en: It sits exactly in the middle of the counting ladder: one, two, many.
normal.cn: 它正好在计数阶梯的中间：单语、双语、多语。

normal.en: The family runs bilingualism, bilingually, bilinguals, multilingual, monolingual.
normal.cn: 同族包括「双语现象」「以双语方式」「双语者」「多语的」「单语的」。

normal.en: A split notice with the same sentence twice is the picture to hold.
normal.cn: 一张左右分栏、同一句话写两遍的告示，是要留住的画面。

abstract.en: Picture two doors side by side, both opening into the same room.
abstract.cn: 想象并排的两道门，都通向同一个房间。

abstract.en: Picture a mind with two indexes to the same world.
abstract.cn: 想象一个头脑，为同一个世界备有两套索引。

abstract.en: Picture a single sentence walking across a thin line and changing its clothes.
abstract.cn: 想象同一句话跨过一条细线，换了一身衣服。

examples.en: Bilingual ballots were introduced after the court ruling.
examples.cn: 法院裁决之后，双语选票开始启用。

examples.en: Children in bilingual programs read in both languages by nine.
examples.cn: 参加双语项目的孩子到九岁已能用两种语言阅读。

examples.en: The bilingual dictionary distinguishes formal from everyday words.
examples.cn: 这本双语词典区分正式词与日常词。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「拜林圭尔」——拜两条舌头所赐，两种话都能说，这就是双语的。

root: 拉丁 bilinguis「双舌的」由表「两次」的成分与 lingua「舌头、语言」构成；罗马用法中亦可指「两面三刀的」，该贬义未被英语保留。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses pair two languages across a person, a sign, a school, a valley, a mind, a dictionary and a law.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项把两种语言配到人、标牌、学校、山谷、心智、词典与法律之上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one sheet folded down the middle, the same sentence on both halves.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张从中间对折的纸，两半写着同一句话。

branches.en: THE COUNT: exactly two languages is the word's whole definition.
branches.cn: 数目：正好两种语言，就是这个词的全部定义。

branches.en: THE SPEAKER: a person can carry both languages through a whole life.
branches.cn: 说话者：一个人可以把两种语言带过一生。

branches.en: WORDS ON PAPER: labels and dictionaries put the two side by side.
branches.cn: 纸上的词：标签与词典把两者并排放置。

branches.en: PLACES THAT TEACH: schools and whole valleys keep two languages alive together.
branches.cn: 教学之地：学校与整条山谷让两种语言一同存活。

branches.en: MIND AND LAW: one brain holds both, and one statute can promise both.
branches.cn: 心智与法律：一个头脑容纳两者，一项法规也能承诺两者。

intro.en: The word is two Latin pieces and an English adjective ending, and each piece also builds a family.
intro.cn: 这个词由两个拉丁成分与一个英语形容词词尾构成，每个成分也都构成一族词。

latinIntro.en: Latin bis 'twice' supplies the counting prefix, Latin lingua the root, and the adjective ending makes the description; the same pieces build multilingual and monolingual.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 bis「两次」提供计数前缀，拉丁 lingua 提供词根，形容词词尾完成描述；同样的成分也构成「多语的」与「单语的」。

items.example: The prefix fixes the count at exactly two.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把数目固定为二。

items.example: The root names what is counted.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根指被计数的东西。

items.example: The ending turns the count into a description.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把数目变成描述。

items.example: The bilingual form served both communities.
items.exampleCN: 这份双语表格服务两个社群。

items.example: Bilingualism began at home, not at school.
items.exampleCN: 双语现象始于家庭，而非学校。

items.example: The ceremony was conducted bilingually.
items.exampleCN: 仪式以双语进行。

items.example: A multilingual city outgrows the pair.
items.exampleCN: 一座多语城市超出了「两种」的范围。

items.example: Monolingual readers needed a translation.
items.exampleCN: 单语读者需要译本。
